rules.rule: SLA definitions with no schedule attached (24x7 applied unintentionally)
rules.what_it_means: SLA definitions have no schedule attached, so duration is measured in calendar time by default.
rules.why_it_matters: A four-hour business-hours commitment enforced as four calendar hours breaches every weekend and overnight. Where the SLA backs a contract, the target being enforced is not the target that was agreed.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition schedule field, contract_sla and sla_definition records
rules.detection_logic: Active SLA definitions with an empty schedule reference
rules.threshold_parameter: Any definition with duration in business-hours intent and no schedule
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state. Whether 24x7 was intended requires the commitment for comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA definition, its duration, absent schedule, the breach distribution by day of week and hour, and the commitment it enforces.
rules.false_positive_guard: 24x7 genuinely intended. Compare against the service commitment before asserting.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — schedule attachment as update set
rules.cross_domain_link: Commercial consequence where SLAs back contracts; joins ITSM-012

rules.rule: Priority bands with no SLA definition at all
rules.what_it_means: One or more priority bands in active use have no SLA definition covering them.
rules.why_it_matters: Records in that band carry no target and appear in no breach calculation. Reported SLA compliance is computed over a subset and presented as the whole.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition start conditions, task priority distribution
rules.detection_logic: Priority bands with record volume whose values satisfy no SLA definition start condition
rules.threshold_parameter: Any band with non-zero volume and no covering definition
rules.evidence_to_show: Bands, volume per band, coverage state, and the compliance figure with and without uncovered volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Band deliberately excluded with documented rationale.

rules.rule: SLA definitions where start, pause and stop conditions can never be simultaneously satisfiable
rules.what_it_means: An SLA definition's start, pause and stop conditions cannot all be satisfied in any reachable state sequence.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA either never starts, never stops, or never pauses. Whichever it is, the resulting data is noise, and the breach numbers derived from it are meaningless.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition start, pause and stop conditions; task state model and reachable transitions
rules.detection_logic: Condition sets evaluated against the state model for reachability; flag definitions with unreachable combinations
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires the task state transition map
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — reachability analysis depends on the state model being complete.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, its three condition sets, the state model, the unreachable combination, and the actual SLA record state distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Conditions satisfiable through a path the analysis did not model.

rules.rule: Overlapping SLA definitions attaching multiple SLAs to the same record
rules.what_it_means: Multiple SLA definitions attach to the same record, with overlapping start conditions.
rules.why_it_matters: The record carries several SLAs, and reporting picks one arbitrarily. Compliance figures differ depending on which definition a report selects.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition start conditions, task_sla records per task
rules.detection_logic: Tasks with more than one active SLA of the same type, and the definitions whose conditions overlap
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the attachment counts and condition overlap.
rules.evidence_to_show: The definitions, their overlapping conditions, the affected task count, and the differing targets each imposes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate layered SLAs, such as response and resolution, which are different types.

rules.rule: SLA definition inactive but still referenced by a commitment or offering
rules.what_it_means: An SLA definition is inactive but is still referenced by a service commitment or offering.
rules.why_it_matters: The commitment points at an enforcement mechanism that is switched off. The offering promises a target with nothing measuring it.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition active flag, commitment and offering references
rules.detection_logic: Commitments or offerings referencing SLA definitions with active=false
rules.evidence_to_show: Commitment, the offering, the referenced definition, its deactivation date, and the record volume that should be under it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Definition superseded by a replacement referenced elsewhere.

rules.rule: Start condition matching on insert only, missing records that qualify later
rules.what_it_means: The SLA start condition evaluates on insert only, so records that qualify later never attach an SLA.
rules.why_it_matters: An incident created as P3 and escalated to P1 carries no P1 SLA. The escalation is invisible to SLA reporting, and the highest-priority work is the least measured.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition start condition and evaluation timing, priority change audit
rules.detection_logic: Definitions whose start condition is insert-only, joined to records that met the condition after insert
rules.threshold_parameter: Any insert-only condition where post-insert qualification occurs
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. The affected record count is exact from audit.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, its condition and timing, the records that qualified later, their escalation timestamps, and the absent SLA records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Condition genuinely only meaningful at insert.
rules.cross_domain_link: Escalated incidents excluded from SLA measurement

rules.rule: Stop condition not covering all resolution or closure states
rules.what_it_means: The stop condition does not cover all resolution and closure states.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA keeps running after the work is done. Breach counts include time after resolution, so the breach figure measures the configuration rather than the service.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition stop conditions, task closure and resolution state set
rules.detection_logic: Definitions whose stop condition omits one or more terminal states with non-zero volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Terminal state set read from the task state model
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, its stop condition, the uncovered terminal states with volume, and the SLA records still running against closed tasks.
rules.false_positive_guard: State deliberately intended to continue accruing.

rules.rule: Pause condition with no corresponding resume path (SLA pauses permanently)
rules.what_it_means: A pause condition has no corresponding resume path, so once paused the SLA never restarts.
rules.why_it_matters: The clock stops permanently. The SLA never breaches and never completes, which makes the record look compliant forever.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition pause conditions, resume logic, task_sla paused duration distribution
rules.detection_logic: Definitions whose pause condition has no complementary resume condition, joined to SLA records paused beyond threshold
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on condition analysis. The affected record count is exact.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, pause and resume conditions, the permanently paused records with durations, and the tasks behind them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Resume handled by a separate mechanism such as a business rule.

rules.rule: Duration defined in calendar time where business time was intended
rules.what_it_means: SLA duration is defined in calendar time where business time was intended.
rules.why_it_matters: Related to PLT-001 but distinct: the schedule may be attached and the duration unit still wrong. Produces targets materially tighter than agreed.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition duration unit and schedule, commitment targets
rules.detection_logic: Definitions whose duration unit is calendar where the attached schedule or commitment implies business time
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — intent inference requires the commitment or the schedule to indicate it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, duration and unit, attached schedule, the commitment target, and the breach pattern by day of week.
rules.false_positive_guard: Calendar time genuinely intended.
rules.cross_domain_link: Enforces a different target than committed

rules.rule: Retroactive start not configured where the process requires it
rules.what_it_means: Retroactive start is not configured where the process requires the SLA to count from an earlier event.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA starts when the record was created rather than when the condition was met. For incidents raised from alerts, the detection-to-creation gap is excluded from the measurement.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition retroactive start configuration, event-to-record creation intervals
rules.detection_logic: Definitions with no retroactive start where a meaningful gap exists between the triggering event and record creation
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — whether retroactive start is required is a process judgement.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, retroactive configuration, the event-to-creation gap distribution, and the SLA time excluded.
rules.false_positive_guard: Process genuinely intends measurement from creation.

rules.rule: SLA workflow attached but never executing
rules.what_it_means: An SLA workflow is attached to a definition and never executes.
rules.why_it_matters: Escalation, notification and breach handling all sit in the workflow. If it never runs, the SLA measures and does nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition workflow attachment, workflow execution records
rules.detection_logic: Definitions with an attached workflow and zero execution records against their SLA instances
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence with non-zero SLA volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, attached workflow, SLA instance volume, zero executions, and the escalations that should have fired.
rules.false_positive_guard: Workflow deliberately inert pending configuration.

rules.rule: SLA definition with no notification or escalation at breach threshold
rules.what_it_means: An SLA definition has no notification or escalation configured at the breach threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Breaches occur silently. The first anyone knows is a report, which is after the fact and too late to act.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition escalation and notification configuration
rules.detection_logic: Active definitions with no escalation or notification at any percentage threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, escalation configuration, breach volume, and the escalation coverage on comparable definitions.
rules.false_positive_guard: Escalation handled by an external monitoring mechanism.

rules.rule: Duplicate SLA definitions differing only in name
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate SLA definitions exist that differ only in name.
rules.why_it_matters: Two definitions enforce the same target on overlapping populations. Reporting splits, and PLT-004 multiple attachment follows.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition conditions, duration, schedule comparison
rules.detection_logic: Definition pairs with matching conditions, duration and schedule but differing names
rules.threshold_parameter: Exact match on the functional fields
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — functional equivalence is exact; whether it is unintended is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both definitions, their functional configuration, the SLA instance volume on each, and the tasks carrying both.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate duplication for reporting segmentation.

rules.rule: SLA conditions referencing fields that no longer exist or have been renamed
rules.what_it_means: SLA conditions reference fields that no longer exist or have been renamed.
rules.why_it_matters: The condition never evaluates true, so the SLA never attaches or never stops. Silent, because a condition referencing a missing field does not error, it simply fails to match.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition condition strings, sys_dictionary field existence
rules.detection_logic: Condition field references with no corresponding dictionary entry on the target table
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, the condition, the missing field, the expected versus actual SLA attachment volume, and the field rename if traceable.
rules.false_positive_guard: Field on a related table resolved by dot-walk that the parser did not handle.

rules.rule: Timezone handling inconsistent between schedule and duration
rules.what_it_means: Timezone handling is inconsistent between the SLA schedule and the duration calculation.
rules.why_it_matters: Targets shift by the timezone offset. For a multi-region estate the same SLA behaves differently depending on where the record originated.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition schedule timezone, duration calculation timezone, task location and user timezone
rules.detection_logic: Definitions where the schedule timezone differs from the calculation basis, or where records span timezones with a single fixed schedule
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on the timezone configuration being fully introspectable.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, schedule timezone, calculation basis, the record distribution by location timezone, and the breach pattern by region.
rules.false_positive_guard: Single-timezone estate, or deliberate fixed-timezone measurement.

rules.rule: SLA definition never reviewed since creation date
rules.what_it_means: An SLA definition has never been reviewed since creation.
rules.why_it_matters: The target was set for an estate and a service model that have since changed. Low severity alone; meaningful alongside the commitment linkage findings.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition creation and update history
rules.detection_logic: Active definitions with no update since creation, above age threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition list with creation date, age, SLA instance volume, and breach rate trend over that period.
rules.false_positive_guard: Stable targets genuinely requiring no revision.

rules.rule: Task SLA records stuck in In Progress beyond maximum possible duration
rules.what_it_means: task_sla records are stuck In Progress beyond the maximum duration the definition could produce.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA engine has lost track of them. They will never breach and never complete, so they are permanently absent from compliance figures.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla state, start time, definition duration and schedule
rules.detection_logic: SLA records In Progress where elapsed time exceeds the maximum possible duration under the definition and schedule
rules.threshold_parameter: Maximum computed from duration plus schedule expansion
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA records with start time, elapsed, the definition maximum, the parent task state, and whether the parent is closed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately long-paused records. Exclude paused time from elapsed.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — SLA repair, then fix the condition causing it

rules.rule: High volume of SLA records in Cancelled state (conditions misfiring)
rules.what_it_means: A high volume of task_sla records sit in Cancelled state, indicating conditions are misfiring.
rules.why_it_matters: SLAs attach and immediately cancel. The record shows no SLA, so it appears unmeasured rather than mismeasured, and nobody investigates.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla state distribution, cancellation timing
rules.detection_logic: Cancelled SLA volume as a share of total, by definition; plus cancellation occurring within seconds of attachment
rules.evidence_to_show: Cancellation volume by definition, the timing distribution, the conditions involved, and the tasks now carrying no SLA.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate cancellation on task cancellation.

rules.rule: SLA attached to records it should not apply to
rules.what_it_means: SLAs are attaching to records they should not apply to.
rules.why_it_matters: Over-attachment inflates the measured population with work that was never in scope. Breach figures include records that should never have carried a target.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla attachment, definition conditions, task attributes
rules.detection_logic: SLA instances on tasks whose attributes fall outside the definition's intended scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Intended scope from the definition description and commitment where available
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — intended scope is partly inferred from the commitment.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, its condition, the out-of-scope tasks with their attributes, and the volume and breach rate for that subset.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scope genuinely broad by design.

rules.rule: Records that should carry an SLA carrying none
rules.what_it_means: Records that should carry an SLA are carrying none.
rules.why_it_matters: The inverse of PLT-019 and the more damaging one. Work that was committed to is not being measured at all, and the compliance figure is computed over a favourable subset.
rules.source_tables_fields: Task population against SLA definition conditions, task_sla attachment
rules.detection_logic: Tasks satisfying a definition's start condition with no corresponding SLA record
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on condition evaluation and attachment check.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, the qualifying tasks with no SLA, the volume, and the compliance figure including and excluding them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Records where the SLA was legitimately cancelled.
rules.cross_domain_link: The compliance figure excludes unmeasured work

rules.rule: Pause duration exceeding active duration at scale (gaming or misconfiguration)
rules.what_it_means: Paused duration exceeds active duration at scale across a definition or a group.
rules.why_it_matters: Most of the elapsed time is not being counted. Either the pause condition is too broad, or pause is being used to manage the metric. Both need investigating and the data cannot distinguish them.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla paused and active duration, distribution by definition and group
rules.detection_logic: SLA records where paused duration exceeds active duration, as a share of volume by definition and group
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the duration comparison. The interpretation requires the pause reasons.
rules.evidence_to_show: Paused versus active duration distribution by definition and group, the pause reasons where captured, and the on-hold state correlation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Workload legitimately dominated by third-party waits.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; joins ITSM-034 and ITSM-043

rules.rule: SLA repair or recalculation jobs run manually and frequently
rules.what_it_means: SLA repair or recalculation jobs are being run manually and frequently.
rules.why_it_matters: Somebody is repeatedly fixing the SLA data by hand. The underlying condition defect is being masked rather than fixed, and the manual repair is unaudited.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA repair job execution records, execution user and frequency
rules.detection_logic: Manual SLA repair executions above frequency threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Repair execution history with users and dates, the SLA records affected each time, and the definitions most frequently repaired.
rules.false_positive_guard: Repair as part of a documented migration.

rules.rule: task\_sla table growth disproportionate to task volume
rules.what_it_means: task_sla table growth is disproportionate to task volume.
rules.why_it_matters: More SLA records than tasks can justify. Indicates multiple attachment, repeated re-attachment, or orphan accumulation, and it carries real query cost.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla row count and growth, task volume
rules.detection_logic: SLA row count per task, trended, against the expected ratio from definition coverage
rules.threshold_parameter: Expected ratio derived from active definition count and coverage
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio. Expected ratio derivation must be stated.
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA-to-task ratio trend, the expected ratio, the definitions contributing most, and the multiple-attachment volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately many definitions per task.
rules.cross_domain_link: Query cost; indicates PLT-004 or PLT-027

rules.rule: SLA breach notifications firing to inactive users or empty groups
rules.what_it_means: SLA breach notifications resolve to inactive users or empty groups.
rules.why_it_matters: The breach fires and nobody is told. The escalation is configured, executes, and reaches nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA escalation notification recipients, sys_user.active, group membership
rules.detection_logic: SLA notification recipients resolving to inactive users or groups with zero active members
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, escalation configuration, resolved recipient state, and the breach volume that fired to nobody.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recipient deactivated with a delegate configured.
rules.cross_domain_link: Silent breach escalation; joins ITSM-011 and DQ-130

rules.rule: SLA percentage calculation producing values outside expected range
rules.what_it_means: SLA percentage calculations produce values outside the expected range.
rules.why_it_matters: Negative percentages or values far above 100 indicate the calculation basis is wrong. Any report built on the percentage is unreliable.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla percentage field distribution
rules.detection_logic: SLA records with percentage below 0 or above a configured ceiling
rules.evidence_to_show: Record count by definition and value range, the duration and schedule configuration for those definitions, and sample records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Extreme but legitimate overruns on a genuinely breached SLA.

rules.rule: SLA attached to closed records still updating
rules.what_it_means: SLA records attached to closed tasks are still updating.
rules.why_it_matters: The task is done and the SLA continues to accrue. Direct consequence of PLT-007, and it inflates breach counts with post-closure time.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla state and update timestamps, parent task state and closure time
rules.detection_logic: SLA records updating after their parent task closure timestamp
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA records with parent closure time, SLA last update, the elapsed post-closure accrual, and the definition stop condition.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate post-closure SLA for a warranty or verification period.

rules.rule: Orphaned task\_sla records pointing to deleted tasks
rules.what_it_means: Orphaned task_sla records point to tasks that no longer exist.
rules.why_it_matters: Table bloat and broken references. Reports joining SLA to task drop these rows silently, so the compliance denominator is quietly wrong.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla task references, task record existence
rules.detection_logic: SLA records whose task sys_id has no corresponding record
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the record exists or it does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Orphan count by definition, the missing task sys_ids, and the deletion events if retained.
rules.false_positive_guard: None. Always a defect.

rules.rule: Service offerings with commitments but no underlying SLA definition
rules.what_it_means: Service offerings carry commitments with no underlying SLA definition enforcing them.
rules.why_it_matters: The offering promises a target and nothing measures it. The commitment is a statement, not a control, and reporting against it is manual or absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: Service offering commitment records, SLA definition linkage
rules.detection_logic: Commitments with no linked or condition-matching SLA definition
rules.evidence_to_show: Offering, commitment target, absent SLA definition, the incident volume under that offering, and the reporting currently produced.
rules.false_positive_guard: Commitment measured through an external mechanism.

rules.rule: SLA definitions not traceable to any service commitment (unaccountable targets)
rules.what_it_means: SLA definitions exist that cannot be traced to any service commitment.
rules.why_it_matters: Targets are being enforced that nobody agreed to. Teams are measured against numbers with no accountable origin, which is where SLA gaming pressure comes from.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definitions, commitment and offering linkage
rules.detection_logic: Active definitions with no traceable commitment or offering
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, its target, SLA instance volume, breach rate, and the absence of commitment lineage.
rules.false_positive_guard: Internal operational targets deliberately not tied to a commitment.

rules.rule: Commitment targets inconsistent with the SLA duration configured to enforce them
rules.what_it_means: The commitment target and the SLA duration configured to enforce it do not match.
rules.why_it_matters: The contract says one number and the system enforces another. Where the SLA is looser, the commitment is unprotected; where tighter, the team is measured against a target nobody agreed.
rules.source_tables_fields: Commitment target values, linked SLA definition duration and schedule
rules.detection_logic: Commitment-SLA pairs where the effective SLA duration under its schedule differs from the commitment target
rules.threshold_parameter: Compare effective duration, not raw duration — schedule expansion matters
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the comparison where both are structured. State the schedule expansion applied.
rules.evidence_to_show: Commitment, its target, the SLA definition, duration, schedule, effective duration, and the difference.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate internal buffer below the external commitment.

rules.rule: Business Critical services with no SLA coverage on any priority
rules.what_it_means: Business Critical services have no SLA coverage on any priority band.
rules.why_it_matters: The services the business cares most about have no measured targets. Whatever is reported about their performance is not derived from an enforced commitment.
rules.source_tables_fields: Service criticality, SLA definition scope, incident volume by service
rules.detection_logic: Business Critical services with incident volume and no SLA definition covering any of their incidents
rules.evidence_to_show: Service, criticality, incident volume, SLA coverage state, and the offerings and commitments attached.
rules.false_positive_guard: Coverage provided by a definition scoped by another attribute.

rules.rule: SLA reporting based on a different definition than the one contractually committed
rules.what_it_means: SLA reporting is based on a different definition than the one contractually committed.
rules.why_it_matters: The report and the contract measure different things. The reported compliance figure is not the figure the contract would produce, and nobody comparing them would know.
rules.source_tables_fields: Reporting SLA definition references, commitment linked definitions
rules.detection_logic: Reports and dashboards referencing SLA definitions that differ from the definitions linked to the relevant commitments
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires both reporting configuration and commitment linkage
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on report configuration being introspectable.
rules.evidence_to_show: The report, the definition it uses, the committed definition, both targets, and the compliance figure each produces.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate internal reporting alongside separate contractual reporting.

rules.rule: Business rules on high-volume tables with no condition (fire on every operation)
rules.what_it_means: Business rules run on high-volume tables with no condition, executing on every insert and update.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule executes hundreds of thousands of times to do something relevant a fraction of the time. This is the most common cause of platform-wide transaction slowdown, and it is entirely avoidable.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script condition field, collection, table row counts and update frequency from audit
rules.detection_logic: Active rules on tables above a volume threshold with empty condition and empty filter
rules.threshold_parameter: Volume threshold configurable; combine row count and update frequency
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. The execution count is computed from table update volume.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, table, row count, update frequency, computed execution count, and the rule's position in slow transaction traces.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rules that genuinely must evaluate every record, such as audit or security logic.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — condition addition as update set, tested in sub-production
rules.cross_domain_link: Leading contributor to PLT-052 and PLT-171

rules.rule: current.update() inside a before rule
rules.what_it_means: A before business rule calls current.update().
rules.why_it_matters: In a before rule the record has not been written yet. Calling update forces a second database write and can trigger the rule again, producing recursion. It is the single clearest anti-pattern in ServiceNow scripting.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script script body, when field
rules.detection_logic: Before rules whose script contains a current.update() call
rules.confidence_basis: 98% — pattern match on the script body; a commented-out occurrence is possible.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the offending line with surrounding context, the table, execution count, and the transaction time attributable.
rules.false_positive_guard: Occurrence inside a comment or a string literal. Parse rather than plain-match.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — corrected script as update set with full diff

rules.rule: GlideRecord query inside a loop
rules.what_it_means: A GlideRecord query is executed inside a loop.
rules.why_it_matters: One query per iteration. On a hundred-row loop that is a hundred database round trips where an encoded query would have been one. Scales linearly with data volume, so it degrades as the estate grows.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script and sys_script_include script bodies, loop and query pattern analysis
rules.detection_logic: Scripts containing a GlideRecord instantiation or query call within a loop construct
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; rank by the rule's execution count
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — static analysis of loop-query nesting; dynamic constructs may be missed.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the offending block, execution count, the table queried, its row count, and the resulting query volume per execution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Loops with a known small fixed bound.
rules.cross_domain_link: Scales with data volume; worsens over time

rules.rule: Synchronous processing that should be asynchronous (before/after where async fits)
rules.what_it_means: Processing runs synchronously in a before or after rule where async would be appropriate.
rules.why_it_matters: The user waits for work that does not need to happen in their transaction. Integration calls, notifications and downstream updates all belong in async.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script when field and script body, operation type analysis
rules.detection_logic: Before and after rules performing operations classified as async-appropriate: outbound calls, bulk updates, notification generation
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — whether an operation is async-appropriate is a judgement encoded in classification.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the operation, its when setting, execution count, and the transaction time attributable to it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Operations that genuinely must complete within the transaction.

rules.rule: Business rules on task or cmdb\_ci base table cascading to all children
rules.what_it_means: Business rules are defined on the task or cmdb_ci base tables, cascading to every child class.
rules.why_it_matters: A rule intended for incidents runs on every task type. A rule intended for servers runs on every CI. The blast radius is orders of magnitude larger than intended and usually nobody realises.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script collection field, class hierarchy expansion, child table volumes
rules.detection_logic: Active rules on base tables, with the child class list and combined row volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Base table set configurable: task, cmdb_ci, and other significant parents
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, base table, the child classes it cascades to with row counts, combined execution volume, and the child classes where it is clearly unintended.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rules genuinely intended to apply across the hierarchy.

rules.rule: Rule with no condition and no filter, running on insert and update
rules.what_it_means: A rule has no condition and no filter and runs on both insert and update.
rules.why_it_matters: The broadest possible execution scope. Related to PLT-033 but applies regardless of table volume, because the pattern itself is the defect.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script condition, filter, insert and update flags
rules.detection_logic: Active rules with empty condition, empty filter, and both insert and update true
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, table, its configuration, execution count, and what the script actually does with the majority of executions.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rules that genuinely must run on all operations.

rules.rule: Query with no setLimit on an unbounded table
rules.what_it_means: A query runs against an unbounded table with no setLimit.
rules.why_it_matters: On a large table this returns everything into memory. It works in development against a thousand rows and fails in production against a million.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies across rules, includes and jobs; query construction analysis; target table row counts
rules.detection_logic: Queries on tables above a row threshold with no setLimit and no restrictive encoded query
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — static analysis of query construction; dynamic query building may be missed.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the query, the target table row count, execution count, and the transaction time and memory profile.
rules.false_positive_guard: Queries whose encoded query is inherently restrictive.

rules.rule: Nested GlideRecord traversal beyond two levels
rules.what_it_means: GlideRecord traversal is nested beyond two levels.
rules.why_it_matters: Queries multiply — a hundred parents, a hundred children each, ten thousand round trips. Beyond two levels the cost becomes unmanageable and the logic becomes unmaintainable.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, nested query depth analysis
rules.detection_logic: Scripts with GlideRecord query nesting depth above threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the nested block, the nesting depth, the tables involved with row counts, and the computed query volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Nesting with tight bounds at each level.

rules.rule: Rule ordering causing dependent rules to execute before their prerequisite
rules.what_it_means: Rule execution order places dependent rules before the rules they depend on.
rules.why_it_matters: The dependent rule runs against data its prerequisite has not yet set. The behaviour is inconsistent and depends on execution order that nobody documented.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script order field, field read and write analysis across rules on the same table
rules.detection_logic: Rule pairs on the same table where one reads a field the other writes, with the reader ordered first
rules.threshold_parameter: Field dependency analysis from script bodies
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — dependency inference from static field read and write analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rule pair, their order values, the dependent field, and the operations each performs on it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Dependency handled by a different mechanism.

rules.rule: Display rules performing writes
rules.what_it_means: A display business rule performs writes.
rules.why_it_matters: Display rules run on form load, for every user, every time. A write there multiplies database load by view count and can produce updates nobody intended.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script when field, script body write operation analysis
rules.detection_logic: Display rules whose script contains update, insert or delete operations
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the write operation, the table, form view volume where available, and the resulting write count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Writes to a scratchpad object rather than a record.
rules.cross_domain_link: Writes multiplied by form view volume

rules.rule: Business rule duplicating logic already in a flow, workflow, or another rule
rules.what_it_means: A business rule duplicates logic already implemented in a flow, a workflow, or another rule.
rules.why_it_matters: The same thing happens twice, or the two implementations diverge and produce conflicting outcomes. Maintenance requires knowing both exist, which nobody does.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, flow and workflow logic, trigger condition and target field overlap
rules.detection_logic: Rules whose trigger conditions and target fields overlap with a flow, workflow or another rule on the same table
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — functional equivalence detection is inferential. Report with both implementations for human comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: The rule, the duplicate implementation, their overlapping triggers and targets, and the execution volume of each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate redundancy with different scope conditions.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — consolidation is an architecture decision

rules.rule: Rule using setWorkflow(false) to suppress downstream logic without justification
rules.what_it_means: A rule uses setWorkflow(false) to suppress downstream logic with no documented justification.
rules.why_it_matters: Suppresses every business rule, flow and engine that would otherwise respond to the change. Frequently the hidden cause of missing relationships, unfired notifications and absent audit entries.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies containing setWorkflow(false), rule description and comments
rules.detection_logic: Scripts calling setWorkflow(false) with no explanatory comment or description
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the suppressing line, the table, execution count, and the downstream logic on that table that is being suppressed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Documented and legitimate suppression, such as bulk data loads.
rules.cross_domain_link: Hidden cause of missing downstream effects including relationships

rules.rule: Recursive rule triggering itself through its own update
rules.what_it_means: A rule triggers itself through its own update, producing recursion.
rules.why_it_matters: Each execution causes another. The platform caps recursion depth, so it does not hang, but it multiplies transaction cost and produces duplicate downstream effects.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, trigger conditions, field write analysis
rules.detection_logic: Rules whose write targets satisfy their own trigger condition
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — self-trigger detection from static condition and write analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, its trigger condition, the fields it writes, the self-satisfying overlap, and the execution count relative to table update volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recursion prevented by a guard within the script.
rules.cross_domain_link: Multiplied execution and duplicate downstream effects

rules.rule: Rule with hardcoded sys\_ids
rules.what_it_means: A rule contains hardcoded sys_ids.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule breaks in any other instance, and on any data refresh. It also makes the dependency invisible to every impact analysis, because a hardcoded sys_id is not a reference.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, sys_id pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Scripts containing 32-character hexadecimal literals matching sys_id format
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — pattern match; a coincidental hex string is possible.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the hardcoded values, the records they resolve to where they exist, and whether they resolve in sub-production.
rules.false_positive_guard: Hex strings that are not sys_ids, such as hashes.
rules.cross_domain_link: Breaks on clone and refresh; hides dependencies

rules.rule: Rule with hardcoded credentials, endpoints or tokens
rules.what_it_means: A rule contains hardcoded credentials, endpoints or tokens.
rules.why_it_matters: Secrets in a script table readable by anyone with script read access and captured in every update set. For a regulated entity this is a reportable exposure, not a code quality observation.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, credential and endpoint pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Scripts containing patterns matching passwords, API keys, tokens, or hardcoded URLs with embedded credentials
rules.threshold_parameter: Pattern set configurable; include base64-encoded basic auth
rules.confidence_basis: 85% on pattern detection. Report location and pattern type, never the value.
rules.evidence_to_show: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — the script, the line, the pattern type. Never reproduce the value, in the finding or the report.
rules.false_positive_guard: Placeholder or example values. Review before escalating, and still never display the value.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — rotation and vault migration require security involvement
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure; route to the security reviewer immediately

rules.rule: gs.sleep() or synchronous wait in a rule
rules.what_it_means: A rule contains gs.sleep() or another synchronous wait.
rules.why_it_matters: Holds a transaction and a semaphore for the duration of the wait. At any volume this exhausts the semaphore pool and degrades the entire instance, not just the affected table.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, sleep and wait pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Scripts containing gs.sleep or equivalent blocking wait calls
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the sleep call and its duration, execution count, and the computed semaphore-hold time per hour.
rules.false_positive_guard: Sleep inside a genuinely bounded and rare administrative script.

rules.rule: Rule performing an outbound HTTP call synchronously
rules.what_it_means: A rule performs an outbound HTTP call synchronously.
rules.why_it_matters: The user transaction waits on an external system. When that system is slow, every affected transaction is slow; when it is down, they fail. The platform's availability becomes the external system's availability.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies, RESTMessage and SOAPMessage instantiation, when field
rules.detection_logic: Synchronous rules containing outbound HTTP calls
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence in before, after or display rules
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — pattern detection of outbound call construction.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, the outbound call and endpoint, when setting, execution count, and the transaction time distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Calls with a tight timeout in a rarely executed path.
rules.cross_domain_link: Couples platform availability to external systems

rules.rule: Rule with empty or commented-out script body but still active
rules.what_it_means: A rule is active with an empty or fully commented-out script body.
rules.why_it_matters: Executes and does nothing. Consumes a rule slot in execution order and confuses anyone reading the configuration.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script script body, active flag
rules.detection_logic: Active rules whose script body is empty or contains only comments
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list, table, execution count, and last modification date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rule temporarily emptied during troubleshooting.

rules.rule: Rule with no description
rules.what_it_means: A business rule has no description.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody knows what it is for. Becomes a problem at upgrade and during incident investigation, which is why it is Low rather than absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script description field
rules.detection_logic: Active rules with empty description
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list with table, creation date, creating user, and execution count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rules where the name is genuinely self-documenting.

rules.rule: Rules contributing measurably to slow transactions, ranked by total time
rules.what_it_means: Business rules are contributing measurably to slow transactions, ranked by total time consumed.
rules.why_it_matters: The ranked list is the actionable output of the entire business rule group. It converts a list of anti-patterns into a prioritised remediation queue ordered by measured impact.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog_transaction slow transaction data, script execution attribution, sys_script records
rules.detection_logic: Rules appearing in slow transaction traces, ranked by total time = average time x execution count
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where transaction data attributes the script. Attribution completeness varies by instance configuration — state it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ranked rule list with average time, execution count, total time, the tables involved, and the anti-patterns each rule contains.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attribution unavailable on instances where transaction data does not identify scripts. Report the limitation rather than guessing.
rules.cross_domain_link: The prioritised remediation queue for PLT-033 to PLT-051

rules.rule: Rule execution count disproportionate to table activity
rules.what_it_means: Rule execution count is disproportionate to the table's actual activity.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule is executing more often than the table changes, which means recursion, cascade, or execution from a parent class. Diagnostic of PLT-037 and PLT-045.
rules.source_tables_fields: Rule execution counts, table update volume from audit
rules.detection_logic: Rules whose execution count materially exceeds the update volume of their target table
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the comparison where execution counts are available.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, execution count, table update volume, the ratio, and whether the rule is on a base table or self-triggering.
rules.false_positive_guard: Execution count including display invocations on a heavily viewed table.

rules.rule: Rules throwing errors in the log, by frequency
rules.what_it_means: Business rules are throwing errors in the log, ranked by frequency.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule is failing and the transaction usually continues. Whatever the rule was meant to do is silently not happening, and the only record is a log entry.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog error entries attributed to scripts, sys_script records
rules.detection_logic: Rules with error counts above threshold in the window, ranked by frequency
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on error counts where log attribution identifies the script.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, error count and class, sample stack traces, execution count, and what fails to happen when it errors.
rules.false_positive_guard: Errors from a transient data condition already resolved.

rules.rule: Rules on tables with high record volume and high update frequency
rules.what_it_means: Rules exist on tables with both high record volume and high update frequency.
rules.why_it_matters: A risk-surface measure rather than a defect. Identifies where any inefficiency will be amplified most, and it is the right place to look first when tuning.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script collection, table row counts and update frequency
rules.detection_logic: Rules on tables above thresholds for both volume and update frequency
rules.evidence_to_show: Table list with row count, update frequency, rule count on each, and the combined execution volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: None — this is a risk-surface measure.
rules.cross_domain_link: Prioritisation input for the business rule group

rules.rule: Rules active but with zero execution in the observation window
rules.what_it_means: Rules are active with zero execution in the observation window.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the condition never matches or the table is dormant. Either way the rule is inert and adds upgrade surface and execution-order complexity.
rules.source_tables_fields: Rule execution records, active flag, window
rules.detection_logic: Active rules with zero executions in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list with table, condition, creation date, and the table's update volume in the window.
rules.false_positive_guard: Seasonal or exception-path rules that legitimately rarely fire.

rules.rule: Rules modified within the last N days correlating with performance degradation
rules.what_it_means: Rules modified recently correlate with a measurable performance degradation.
rules.why_it_matters: Direct change-to-performance attribution. Turns a vague slowdown complaint into a specific object and a specific date.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script update timestamps, transaction performance trend, correlation analysis
rules.detection_logic: Rules modified within the window whose modification date aligns with a transaction time increase on their table
rules.threshold_parameter: Window configurable; requires transaction data before and after
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — temporal correlation is strong evidence, not proof. State the alignment.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, modification date and user, the transaction time trend before and after, and the update set carrying the change.
rules.false_positive_guard: Coincidental performance change from another cause.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — revert or correct via update set

rules.rule: Business rules created in global scope where a scoped app exists
rules.what_it_means: Business rules are created in global scope where a scoped application exists for that functionality.
rules.why_it_matters: Global scope has no boundary. The rule can affect anything, is not covered by the scoped app's governance, and is invisible in the application's dependency view.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script scope, scoped application inventory and their table coverage
rules.detection_logic: Global-scope rules on tables owned by or heavily used by an existing scoped application
rules.threshold_parameter: Ownership inference from table scope and application file membership
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — the inference that the rule belongs in the scoped app is a judgement.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, its scope, the table, the scoped application covering that table, and the rules already in that app.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rule genuinely cross-cutting and correctly global.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — scope migration is an architecture decision

rules.rule: Rules modifying OOB tables without a scoped application boundary
rules.what_it_means: Rules modify out-of-box tables with no scoped application boundary.
rules.why_it_matters: Direct modification of platform tables from global scope. Maximum upgrade collision risk and no containment if the logic misbehaves.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script scope and collection, OOB table identification
rules.detection_logic: Global-scope rules writing to OOB tables
rules.threshold_parameter: OOB table set from the base install
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on scope and collection. Write detection from script analysis at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, table, the writes performed, scope, and the upgrade collision surface it creates.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately required platform extension.

rules.rule: Rules created directly in production (no update set lineage)
rules.what_it_means: Rules were created directly in production with no update set lineage.
rules.why_it_matters: The change bypassed the entire release process. There is no test evidence, no approval, no rollback path, and no record of what the instance looked like before.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script records, sys_update_xml lineage, creation instance indicators
rules.detection_logic: Rules with no corresponding update set record and creation timestamps outside deployment windows
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report count and trend
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — absence of lineage is strong evidence; update set records can be cleared.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list with creation date and user, absent update set lineage, and the change records in the same window for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Update set records purged by retention policy. Check the retention window.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITSM-106; direct change control bypass

rules.rule: Rules with no owner, or owner is an inactive user
rules.what_it_means: Rules have no owner, or the owner is an inactive user.
rules.why_it_matters: When the rule causes a problem, nobody knows who to ask. The knowledge left with the person.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script created_by and owner fields, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Active rules whose owner or creator is inactive, or with no owner field populated
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list with owner state, creation date, table, and execution count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership held at the application level.

rules.rule: Rules with no linked change record
rules.what_it_means: Rules have no linked change record.
rules.why_it_matters: The rule exists with no traceable authorisation. Distinct from PLT-060 because an update set may exist without a change behind it.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script records, update set to change record linkage
rules.detection_logic: Rules whose update set has no linked change request
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, its update set, the absent change linkage, creation date, and the change records in that window.
rules.false_positive_guard: Changes linked at a batch level rather than per update set.

rules.rule: Rules overriding OOB rules of the same name
rules.what_it_means: Custom rules override out-of-box rules of the same name.
rules.why_it_matters: The OOB rule is replaced rather than extended. Every upgrade that improves the OOB rule will collide, and the improvement will be skipped.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script records, OOB rule inventory, name and table matching
rules.detection_logic: Custom rules with the same name and table as an OOB rule
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — name and table match is strong; deliberate replacement is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Custom rule, the OOB rule it shadows, the functional difference, and the skipped update history for that record.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate and documented replacement.

rules.rule: Rule count growth trend per table
rules.what_it_means: The business rule count per table is growing over time.
rules.why_it_matters: Each addition increases execution cost and order complexity. The trend matters more than the count, because it indicates whether the estate is accumulating logic faster than it retires it.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script counts per table across snapshots
rules.detection_logic: Rule count per table, trended
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on counts. Trend confidence from snapshot count.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule count by table with trend, the tables growing fastest, and the execution cost per table.
rules.false_positive_guard: Active development on a new application.

rules.rule: Client-callable Script Includes with no ACL protection
rules.what_it_means: Client-callable Script Includes have no ACL protection.
rules.why_it_matters: Any authenticated user can invoke them from the browser with arbitrary parameters. If the include queries or writes data, the ACL model is bypassed entirely. This is the most common ServiceNow privilege escalation path.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include client_callable flag, access field, sys_security_acl coverage
rules.detection_logic: Client-callable includes with no ACL protection and no role restriction
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; escalate where the include performs queries or writes
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. Risk severity from the operations the include performs.
rules.evidence_to_show: Include, its client-callable and access configuration, the operations it performs, the tables it touches, and its callers.
rules.false_positive_guard: Include that returns only non-sensitive static data.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — ACL and role restriction as update set
rules.cross_domain_link: Primary privilege escalation path; route to security

rules.rule: Script Include accessible from all application scopes unnecessarily
rules.what_it_means: A Script Include is accessible from all application scopes where it need not be.
rules.why_it_matters: Any scoped application can call it. Broadens the attack and dependency surface, and makes the include impossible to change safely because callers are unknown.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include access field, actual cross-scope call analysis
rules.detection_logic: Includes with all-scopes access whose actual callers are confined to one or two scopes
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — caller analysis from static reference detection may miss dynamic invocation.
rules.evidence_to_show: Include, its access setting, the scopes actually calling it, and the operations it performs.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely shared utility includes.

rules.rule: Script Include with no access restriction performing privileged operations
rules.what_it_means: A Script Include performs privileged operations with no access restriction.
rules.why_it_matters: Privileged logic callable by anything. Combined with PLT-065 this is a complete bypass of the platform's access model.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include access configuration, privileged operation detection in script body
rules.detection_logic: Includes performing elevated operations (GlideRecord on restricted tables, role manipulation, credential access) with no access restriction
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — privileged operation detection from static analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Include, the privileged operations, its access configuration, callers, and the tables and records reachable through it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Include restricted by a mechanism outside the access field.

rules.rule: Duplicate Script Includes with near-identical logic
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate Script Includes exist with near-identical logic.
rules.why_it_matters: Two implementations of the same function. A fix applied to one leaves the other wrong, and which one a given caller uses is arbitrary.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include script bodies, similarity analysis
rules.detection_logic: Include pairs with script similarity above threshold
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — similarity is exact, the conclusion that duplication is unintended is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both includes, their similarity, their callers, creation dates, and the functional differences.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate versioned copies during a migration.

rules.rule: Script Include never referenced by anything
rules.what_it_means: A Script Include is never referenced by anything.
rules.why_it_matters: Dead code. Adds upgrade review surface and makes the codebase harder to reason about.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include records, reference detection across scripts, flows and workflows
rules.detection_logic: Includes with no detected references and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 180 days; caller detection must cover dynamic invocation patterns
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — dynamic invocation by name may not be detected. State this before recommending removal.
rules.evidence_to_show: Include list, creation date, size, and the reference scan scope applied.
rules.false_positive_guard: Dynamic invocation by name that static analysis cannot detect. Never bulk-delete on this rule alone.

rules.rule: Script Include exceeding a size threshold (unmaintainable)
rules.what_it_means: A Script Include exceeds a size threshold that makes it unmaintainable.
rules.why_it_matters: Large monolithic includes are hard to test, hard to change safely, and usually contain several unrelated functions.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include script body length and function count
rules.detection_logic: Includes above line or character threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Include list with size, function count, caller count, and modification frequency.
rules.false_positive_guard: Generated code.

rules.rule: Recursive or deeply nested include chains
rules.what_it_means: Script Include chains are recursive or nested beyond a reasonable depth.
rules.why_it_matters: Each level adds call overhead and makes failure diagnosis harder. Recursion risks stack exhaustion.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script Include cross-reference graph, cycle and depth analysis
rules.detection_logic: Include call graphs with cycles, or depth above threshold
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — call graph built from static references.
rules.evidence_to_show: The chain or cycle with each include, the entry points, and the execution volume through it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate recursion with a bounded guard.

rules.rule: Hardcoded credentials or endpoints
rules.what_it_means: A Script Include contains hardcoded credentials or endpoints.
rules.why_it_matters: Same exposure as PLT-047, in a more widely callable place. Script Includes are typically readable by more roles than business rules.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include script bodies, credential and endpoint pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Includes containing credential, token or embedded-credential URL patterns
rules.confidence_basis: 85% on pattern detection. Report location and type only.
rules.evidence_to_show: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — include, line, pattern type. Never reproduce the value.
rules.false_positive_guard: Placeholder values. Review without displaying.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — rotation and vault migration with security involvement
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure; route to security immediately

rules.rule: Script Include throwing uncaught exceptions
rules.what_it_means: Script Includes throw uncaught exceptions.
rules.why_it_matters: The calling transaction fails or continues in an undefined state. Because includes are shared, one defect propagates to every caller.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog errors attributed to includes, script body exception handling analysis
rules.detection_logic: Includes with error counts above threshold, or with no try-catch around fallible operations
rules.threshold_parameter: Report both the observed errors and the structural absence of handling
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on observed errors. 85% on structural handling analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Include, error count and class, sample traces, the callers affected, and the handling state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Exceptions deliberately propagated to callers that handle them.

rules.rule: Overriding an OOB Script Include
rules.what_it_means: A custom Script Include overrides an out-of-box Script Include.
rules.why_it_matters: Platform logic replaced. Every upgrade improvement to that include is skipped, and the custom version accumulates divergence from the platform.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_include records, OOB inventory, name matching
rules.detection_logic: Custom includes with the same name as an OOB include
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — name match within scope is strong evidence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Custom include, the OOB include shadowed, the functional difference, caller count, and skipped update history.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate documented replacement.

rules.rule: Synchronous GlideAjax or getReference without callback
rules.what_it_means: Client scripts use synchronous GlideAjax or getReference without a callback.
rules.why_it_matters: The browser freezes until the server responds. Every form load or field change carries the full server round trip with the UI locked. The most visible performance defect a user experiences.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client script bodies, GlideAjax and getReference call analysis
rules.detection_logic: Client scripts with getXMLWait, or getReference called without a callback parameter
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — pattern detection of synchronous call forms.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the synchronous call, the table and form, the field it fires on, and the form view volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Calls in an administrative form with negligible volume.

rules.rule: DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, jQuery)
rules.what_it_means: Client scripts manipulate the DOM directly using document.getElementById or jQuery.
rules.why_it_matters: Bypasses the platform's UI API. Breaks on every UI framework change and on every upgrade, and behaves differently across form views.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client script bodies, DOM access pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Client scripts containing direct DOM access or jQuery selectors
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the DOM access, the table and form, and the UI framework versions it must survive.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legacy scripts on forms scheduled for retirement.
rules.cross_domain_link: Breaks at every UI framework change and upgrade

rules.rule: Client script running on load performing server round-trips
rules.what_it_means: A client script runs on form load and performs server round trips.
rules.why_it_matters: Every form open incurs the round trip. Multiplied by view volume this is a substantial and entirely avoidable load, and the user waits for all of it.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client type and script body, server call detection
rules.detection_logic: onLoad client scripts containing GlideAjax, GlideRecord or getReference calls
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; rank by form view volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the server calls, the table and form, view volume, and the resulting server call count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Data genuinely required at load with no alternative.
rules.cross_domain_link: Load cost multiplied by view volume

rules.rule: Client script duplicating logic available in a UI Policy
rules.what_it_means: A client script duplicates logic that a UI Policy could implement declaratively.
rules.why_it_matters: Scripted where configuration would do. Harder to maintain, slower to execute, and invisible to anyone reviewing UI Policies.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client script bodies, UI policy capability mapping
rules.detection_logic: Client scripts performing only field visibility, mandatory or read-only manipulation
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the operations it performs, the equivalent UI Policy configuration, and the table and form.
rules.false_positive_guard: Logic with conditions a UI Policy cannot express.

rules.rule: Multiple onChange scripts on the same field
rules.what_it_means: Multiple onChange client scripts fire on the same field.
rules.why_it_matters: Execution order between them is not guaranteed and they may contradict each other. Behaviour becomes inconsistent in ways that are very hard to reproduce.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client field and type, grouping by table and field
rules.detection_logic: Table and field combinations with more than one active onChange script
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence with more than one
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, the scripts firing on it, their order values where set, and what each does.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scripts with mutually exclusive conditions.

rules.rule: Client script with no condition, running on every form load
rules.what_it_means: A client script has no condition and runs on every form load.
rules.why_it_matters: Executes regardless of relevance. Individually small, cumulatively significant on forms with many scripts.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client condition field and type
rules.detection_logic: onLoad client scripts with empty condition
rules.evidence_to_show: Script list by table and form, form view volume, and the scripts' execution content.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scripts that genuinely must run on every load.

rules.rule: Client script referencing fields not present on the form
rules.what_it_means: A client script references fields that are not present on the form.
rules.why_it_matters: The reference resolves to nothing. The script either errors in the browser console or silently does nothing, and the intended behaviour is absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client script bodies, form layout field lists
rules.detection_logic: Client script field references absent from the form layouts the script applies to
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — field references may be conditional or dot-walked.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the referenced field, the form layouts, and the behaviour that does not occur.
rules.false_positive_guard: Fields present on some views and not others.

rules.rule: Client script not compatible with the current UI framework
rules.what_it_means: Client scripts are not compatible with the current UI framework.
rules.why_it_matters: Written for a prior UI and running, or failing, on the current one. The failure is often partial, which is worse than total because it is not noticed.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client script bodies, deprecated API and framework pattern detection, instance UI configuration
rules.detection_logic: Client scripts using APIs deprecated or unsupported in the current UI framework
rules.threshold_parameter: Deprecated API set per UI framework version
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on the deprecation list for the instance's UI version.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the incompatible API, the current UI framework, the forms affected, and the browser error volume where available.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scripts scoped to a legacy UI still in use.
rules.cross_domain_link: Partial silent failure after UI changes

rules.rule: Client-side validation with no matching server-side enforcement
rules.what_it_means: Client-side validation exists with no matching server-side enforcement.
rules.why_it_matters: Anyone with API, import set or web service access bypasses it entirely. The validation is a UX convenience presented as a control, and in a regulated entity that distinction matters.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script_client validation logic, data policy and business rule server-side equivalents
rules.detection_logic: Client-side validation rules with no corresponding data policy or server-side business rule on the same field
rules.threshold_parameter: Field-level comparison between client validation and server enforcement
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — equivalence detection between client and server logic is inferential.
rules.evidence_to_show: Client validation, the field, the absent server-side enforcement, and the API and import volume writing to that field.
rules.false_positive_guard: Validation genuinely UX-only with no control intent.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — data policy as update set

rules.rule: UI Policy enforcing mandatory fields with no corresponding Data Policy (API bypass)
rules.what_it_means: A UI Policy enforces mandatory fields with no corresponding Data Policy.
rules.why_it_matters: The field is mandatory in the browser and nullable through the API, import sets and web services. Every integration writing to that table can create records the UI would have rejected.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy mandatory actions, data policy coverage for the same fields
rules.detection_logic: UI policy mandatory field actions with no matching data policy rule
rules.evidence_to_show: UI policy, the mandatory fields, absent data policy coverage, and the record count created through API and import with those fields empty.
rules.false_positive_guard: Field deliberately mandatory only for interactive users.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — data policy as update set
rules.cross_domain_link: The most common bypassable-control pattern in ServiceNow

rules.rule: Conflicting UI Policies on the same field
rules.what_it_means: Conflicting UI Policies act on the same field.
rules.why_it_matters: One makes it mandatory, another makes it read-only. The outcome depends on execution order, which produces behaviour users describe as random.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy actions grouped by table and field, action conflict detection
rules.detection_logic: Field-level action sets containing contradictory actions across active policies
rules.threshold_parameter: Conflict matrix: mandatory vs read-only, visible vs hidden
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, the conflicting policies, their conditions and order, and the contradictory actions.
rules.false_positive_guard: Policies with mutually exclusive conditions.

rules.rule: Data Policy not applied to import sets or web services where it should be
rules.what_it_means: Data Policies are not applied to import sets or web services where they should be.
rules.why_it_matters: The data policy exists and is scoped to exclude the paths most likely to introduce bad data. Integrations bypass the validation that interactive users cannot.
rules.source_tables_fields: Data policy apply-to configuration for import sets and SOAP/REST
rules.detection_logic: Data policies with import set or web service application disabled
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence where those paths carry volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Data policy, its apply-to configuration, the import and API volume on that table, and the records created that would have failed the policy.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate exclusion for a controlled bulk load.

rules.rule: UI Policy with a script where declarative configuration suffices
rules.what_it_means: A UI Policy uses a script where declarative configuration would suffice.
rules.why_it_matters: Harder to read, harder to maintain, and invisible to anyone reviewing the declarative configuration. Low consequence, real accumulation.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy script fields, action equivalence analysis
rules.detection_logic: UI policies with scripts performing only actions expressible declaratively
rules.evidence_to_show: Policy, its script, the declarative equivalent, and the table and form.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scripts performing logic beyond the declarative model.

rules.rule: UI Policy with no condition
rules.what_it_means: A UI Policy has no condition and applies unconditionally.
rules.why_it_matters: Applies on every form load for every record. Usually indicates the policy was meant to be conditional and the condition was never added.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy condition field
rules.detection_logic: Active UI policies with empty condition
rules.evidence_to_show: Policy list with table, form, its actions, and form view volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Policies genuinely intended to apply always.

rules.rule: Data Policy inactive but relied upon by process documentation
rules.what_it_means: A Data Policy is inactive while process documentation relies on it.
rules.why_it_matters: The control is documented as present and is switched off. For audit purposes this is worse than never having had it, because the documentation asserts a control that does not exist.
rules.source_tables_fields: Data policy active flag, references from knowledge and process documentation where available
rules.detection_logic: Inactive data policies on fields that process documentation or a control register references
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires documentation or control register linkage
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on documentation being introspectable or supplied.
rules.evidence_to_show: Policy, its deactivation date and user, the documentation referencing it, and the records created since that would have failed it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Policy superseded by an equivalent control.
rules.cross_domain_link: Documented control that does not exist

rules.rule: Field mandatory in UI Policy but nullable in dictionary
rules.what_it_means: A field is mandatory in a UI Policy but nullable in the dictionary.
rules.why_it_matters: The narrower form of PLT-084, at the dictionary level. The database will accept null regardless of what the UI enforces.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy mandatory actions, sys_dictionary mandatory attribute
rules.detection_logic: Fields mandatory in an active UI policy with dictionary mandatory false and no data policy
rules.threshold_parameter: Field-level comparison across all three layers
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, UI policy state, dictionary state, data policy state, and the null record count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Conditional mandatory that the dictionary cannot express.
rules.cross_domain_link: Enforcement gap at the dictionary layer

rules.rule: Three generations of automation (business rule, workflow, flow) performing the same function
rules.what_it_means: Three generations of automation — business rule, legacy workflow, and Flow Designer — perform the same function on the same table.
rules.why_it_matters: The estate has accumulated logic without retiring any. Nobody knows which one actually governs the outcome, and changing behaviour requires finding all three. This is the single most common source of unexplained platform behaviour.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_script, wf_workflow, sys_hub_flow trigger conditions and target fields on the same table
rules.detection_logic: Tables where business rules, workflows and flows all trigger on overlapping conditions and write overlapping fields
rules.threshold_parameter: Overlap analysis across all three mechanisms
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — functional overlap detection is inferential. Report all three implementations for human comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, the three implementations with their triggers and targets, execution volumes, and the overlapping fields.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate layering with clearly separated scope.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — consolidation is an architecture programme, not a fix
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of unexplained platform behaviour

rules.rule: Legacy Workflow still active where Flow Designer equivalents exist
rules.what_it_means: Legacy Workflow remains active where Flow Designer equivalents exist.
rules.why_it_matters: Legacy Workflow is maintenance-mode technology. Running critical automation on it is accumulating debt against a deadline nobody has set but that will arrive.
rules.source_tables_fields: wf_workflow active versions and execution volume, sys_hub_flow coverage of the same functions
rules.detection_logic: Active workflows with execution volume where equivalent flow capability exists
rules.threshold_parameter: Equivalence assessment by function and trigger
