rules.evidence_to_show: Workflow, execution volume, the table and trigger, the equivalent flow capability, and the migration complexity indicators.
rules.false_positive_guard: Workflows using capabilities Flow Designer does not yet cover.

rules.rule: Flows and workflows both triggering on the same table and condition
rules.what_it_means: Flows and workflows both trigger on the same table and condition.
rules.why_it_matters: Both execute. Either the work happens twice or the two produce conflicting outcomes, and which one wins depends on timing.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow and wf_workflow trigger conditions by table
rules.detection_logic: Table and condition combinations with both an active flow and an active workflow triggering
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, the flow and workflow, their conditions, execution volumes, and the fields each writes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate parallel operation during a migration cutover.

rules.rule: Flow with no error handling path
rules.what_it_means: A flow has no error handling path.
rules.why_it_matters: When a step fails the flow stops silently. The record is left mid-process, the user is not told, and there is no queue of failures anyone monitors.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow logic, error handling step presence
rules.detection_logic: Active flows with no error handling or failure path configured
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; escalate for flows on user-facing or integration paths
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow, its steps, absent error handling, execution volume, failure count, and the records currently stuck mid-flow.
rules.false_positive_guard: Trivial flows where failure is inconsequential.

rules.rule: Flow referencing a deleted or inactive object
rules.what_it_means: A flow references an object that has been deleted or made inactive.
rules.why_it_matters: The flow fails at that step, every time it reaches it. Silent until somebody notices the outcome is missing.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow step references, target object existence and state
rules.detection_logic: Flow step references to records, tables, fields or actions that no longer exist or are inactive
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow, the step, the missing reference, execution volume, failure count since the reference broke, and the records affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Reference in a conditional branch never reached.

rules.rule: Flow stuck in an executing state beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: Flow contexts are stuck in an executing state beyond any reasonable duration.
rules.why_it_matters: The flow never completes. The record sits mid-process indefinitely and the context table accumulates.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_flow_context state and duration
rules.detection_logic: Flow contexts in an executing state beyond duration threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold configurable; default 24 hours for non-wait flows
rules.evidence_to_show: Contexts by flow with duration, the step they are stuck at, the records involved, and their business state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Flows with legitimate long waits, such as approvals. Exclude wait steps.
rules.cross_domain_link: Records stuck mid-process; context table growth

rules.rule: Flow execution failure rate above threshold
rules.what_it_means: Flow execution failure rate exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The automation is unreliable. Users and downstream processes receive inconsistent outcomes with no pattern they can predict.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_flow_context outcome distribution by flow
rules.detection_logic: Flows with failure rate above threshold, ranked by failure volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow, execution and failure counts, failure rate, the failing steps, and the records affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Flows where failure is an expected outcome for some inputs.

rules.rule: Flow triggered on every insert with no condition
rules.what_it_means: A flow triggers on every insert with no condition.
rules.why_it_matters: Executes for every record regardless of relevance. Flow execution is heavier than a business rule, so the cost per unnecessary execution is higher.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow trigger configuration
rules.detection_logic: Flows with record-created triggers and empty conditions on tables above a volume threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow, its trigger, the table and insert volume, execution count, and the proportion of executions that take the meaningful branch.
rules.false_positive_guard: Flows that genuinely apply to all records.

rules.rule: Subflow recursion
rules.what_it_means: Subflow calls form a recursive cycle.
rules.why_it_matters: Each invocation calls back into the chain. Execution multiplies and can exhaust the flow engine, affecting unrelated automation.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow subflow call graph, cycle detection
rules.detection_logic: Subflow call graphs containing cycles
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — call graph from static flow logic.
rules.evidence_to_show: The cycle with each flow, the entry point, execution volume, and the context accumulation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Bounded recursion with a documented guard.

rules.rule: Flow with hardcoded credentials or endpoints
rules.what_it_means: A flow contains hardcoded credentials or endpoints.
rules.why_it_matters: Same exposure as PLT-047 and PLT-072, in flow logic. Flow definitions are frequently exported and shared, which widens the exposure further.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow step inputs and script steps, credential and endpoint pattern detection
rules.detection_logic: Flow steps containing credential, token or embedded-credential URL patterns
rules.confidence_basis: 85% on pattern detection. Report location and type only.
rules.evidence_to_show: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — flow, step, pattern type. Never reproduce the value.
rules.false_positive_guard: Placeholder values in an inactive flow.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — rotation and vault migration with security involvement
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure; route to security immediately

rules.rule: Flow with no owner or inactive owner
rules.what_it_means: A flow has no owner, or the owner is inactive.
rules.why_it_matters: When it fails, nobody knows who owns the logic. Flows are typically more complex than rules, so the knowledge loss is greater.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow owner and created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Active flows with empty owner or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow list with owner state, execution volume, failure rate, and creation date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership held at application level.

rules.rule: Orphaned flows with no trigger and no caller
rules.what_it_means: Orphaned flows exist with no trigger and no caller.
rules.why_it_matters: Cannot execute. Adds upgrade review surface and clutters the flow designer for the people maintaining the real ones.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow trigger configuration, subflow caller references
rules.detection_logic: Flows with no trigger and no references as a subflow
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — dynamic subflow invocation may not be detected.
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow list with creation date, size, and the reference scan scope applied.
rules.false_positive_guard: Flows invoked dynamically or through an API.

rules.rule: Workflow versions accumulating without cleanup
rules.what_it_means: Workflow versions accumulate with no cleanup.
rules.why_it_matters: Each published change creates a version and they are never removed. Table growth, slower workflow loading, and a version list nobody can navigate.
rules.source_tables_fields: wf_workflow_version counts per workflow
rules.detection_logic: Workflows with version counts above threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Workflow, version count, the active version, creation dates, and the table size contribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Versions retained deliberately for audit.

rules.rule: Flow performing synchronous integration calls in a user-facing path
rules.what_it_means: A flow performs synchronous integration calls in a user-facing path.
rules.why_it_matters: The user waits for an external system inside their own transaction. Same defect as PLT-049 in the flow engine, and flows make it easier to introduce accidentally.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_hub_flow step types and execution mode, trigger type
rules.detection_logic: Flows with synchronous outbound integration steps triggered from user-facing operations
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — step type and mode from flow introspection.
rules.evidence_to_show: Flow, the integration step and endpoint, its execution mode, the trigger, and the transaction time distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Calls with tight timeouts on a rarely used path.
rules.cross_domain_link: Couples user transactions to external availability

rules.rule: Long-running flow contexts accumulating in the context table
rules.what_it_means: Long-running flow contexts accumulate in the context table.
rules.why_it_matters: Table growth and engine load. Related to PLT-096 but measured as accumulation rather than per-record, so it catches the slow build-up that individual stuck contexts do not reveal.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_flow_context row count, age distribution, growth trend
rules.detection_logic: Context table growth rate and the age distribution of non-terminal contexts
rules.evidence_to_show: Context count by flow and state, age distribution, growth trend, and table size.
rules.false_positive_guard: Long-running approval flows that legitimately hold contexts.

rules.rule: Scheduled jobs overlapping their own next execution (never completing)
rules.what_it_means: Scheduled jobs overlap their own next execution — the job is still running when it is scheduled to start again.
rules.why_it_matters: The job never completes a full cycle. Executions stack, the queue grows, and each run competes with the previous one for the same resources.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto schedule intervals, execution start and end timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Jobs whose average or maximum duration exceeds their scheduled interval
rules.threshold_parameter: Compare against both average and maximum duration
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, interval, duration distribution, overlap frequency, and the concurrent execution count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Jobs with built-in concurrency guards.

rules.rule: Jobs clustered in the same window causing contention
rules.what_it_means: Scheduled jobs cluster in the same execution window, causing contention.
rules.why_it_matters: Twenty jobs at midnight compete for the same worker threads and database capacity. Each takes longer than it would alone, and the aggregate can push past the maintenance window.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto schedule times, execution duration and concurrency analysis
rules.detection_logic: Time windows with job concurrency above threshold, with the aggregate duration
rules.evidence_to_show: Job distribution by scheduled time, the clustered windows, aggregate duration, and the transaction performance during those windows.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate clustering with adequate capacity.

rules.rule: Job with a query that scans an unbounded table
rules.what_it_means: A scheduled job runs a query that scans an unbounded table.
rules.why_it_matters: Same defect as PLT-039, with the additional property that it runs unattended on a schedule. Failures and slowdowns are invisible until the window is missed.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto_script script bodies, query construction, target table row counts
rules.detection_logic: Job scripts with queries on large tables and no setLimit or restrictive encoded query
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, the query, the target table row count, execution duration trend, and the memory profile.
rules.false_positive_guard: Queries with inherently restrictive encoded queries.

rules.rule: Job execution duration trending upward toward its interval
rules.what_it_means: Job execution duration is trending upward toward its scheduled interval.
rules.why_it_matters: Predictable future failure. The job works until the day duration crosses interval, then PLT-106 begins and the cause is not obvious.
rules.source_tables_fields: Job execution duration across runs, trend analysis, scheduled interval
rules.detection_logic: Jobs with positive duration trend projected to exceed interval within the horizon
rules.threshold_parameter: Horizon default 90 days; requires at least 5 runs
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from run count and variance. State the projection.
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, duration trend, interval, projected crossover date, and the data volume driving the growth.
rules.false_positive_guard: Duration growth from a one-time data load.

rules.rule: Job failing repeatedly with no alerting
rules.what_it_means: A job fails repeatedly with no alerting configured.
rules.why_it_matters: The job stops doing its work and nobody is told. Whatever it maintained — archival, reconciliation, notification — silently stops.
rules.source_tables_fields: Job execution outcomes, failure counts, alerting configuration
rules.detection_logic: Jobs with failure rate above threshold and no failure alerting or notification
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, failure count and rate, error class, absent alerting, and what the job maintains.
rules.false_positive_guard: Failures monitored through an external mechanism.

rules.rule: Job active but with no execution record
rules.what_it_means: A job is active with no execution record at all.
rules.why_it_matters: Scheduled and never running. Either the trigger is broken or the job was never properly activated, and whatever it was meant to do has never happened.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto active flag, sys_trigger records, execution history
rules.detection_logic: Active jobs with no execution records and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 30 days or 3 intervals, whichever is longer
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, its schedule, creation date, the trigger record state, and what it was intended to do.
rules.false_positive_guard: Jobs with a future start date.

rules.rule: Job performing record deletion with no archival
rules.what_it_means: A job performs record deletion with no archival.
rules.why_it_matters: Data is destroyed on a schedule with no recovery path. Where the data is subject to retention obligations this is a compliance exposure as well as an operational one.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto_script script bodies, delete operation detection, archival configuration
rules.detection_logic: Jobs performing deleteMultiple or deleteRecord with no corresponding archival step
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — delete operation detection from script analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, the delete operation, the target table and query, the volume deleted per run, and the retention policy for that table.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deletion of genuinely transient data with a documented policy.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — deletion review requires data ownership input
rules.cross_domain_link: Irrecoverable data loss; DPDP retention relevance

rules.rule: Job with no owner or inactive owner
rules.what_it_means: A job has no owner, or the owner is an inactive user.
rules.why_it_matters: When it fails, nobody knows what it does or whether it matters. Jobs are less visible than rules, so the knowledge loss is more complete.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysauto owner and created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Active jobs with empty owner or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.evidence_to_show: Job list with owner state, schedule, last execution, and what it operates on.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership at the application level.

rules.rule: Job running more frequently than its output is consumed
rules.what_it_means: A job runs more frequently than its output is consumed.
rules.why_it_matters: Hourly generation of a report read weekly. Pure waste, and it competes for capacity with jobs that matter.
rules.source_tables_fields: Job schedule interval, output consumption indicators such as report views or downstream record creation
rules.detection_logic: Jobs whose execution frequency materially exceeds their output consumption rate
rules.threshold_parameter: Consumption measurement depends on the job type; state the method
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — consumption inference varies by job type and is the weakest part of this rule.
rules.evidence_to_show: Job, interval, output type, consumption rate, and the execution cost per run.
rules.false_positive_guard: Output consumed through a channel not measurable.

rules.rule: Event queue depth beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: The event queue depth exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Events are queued rather than processed. Notifications, script actions and downstream automation all lag by the queue depth, and during an incident that lag is when it matters most.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysevent queue depth and age aggregates
rules.detection_logic: Event queue depth and oldest-event age against thresholds
rules.threshold_parameter: Age is the more meaningful threshold; default 10 minutes
rules.evidence_to_show: Queue depth and age trend, event type distribution, processing rate versus creation rate, and the consumers affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient backlog during a known bulk operation.

rules.rule: Events registered with no script action or notification consuming them
rules.what_it_means: Events are registered and fired with no script action or notification consuming them.
rules.why_it_matters: The event is generated, queued and processed to no effect. Pure queue load with no function.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysevent_register records, sysevent_script_action and notification consumers, event fire volume
rules.detection_logic: Registered events with fire volume and no active consumer
rules.evidence_to_show: Event, fire volume, absent consumers, and the queue load it contributes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Events consumed by an external subscriber.

rules.rule: Event flooding from a single source
rules.what_it_means: Event flooding from a single source.
rules.why_it_matters: One source dominates the queue and delays everything else. Usually a misconfigured rule or integration firing events in a loop.
rules.source_tables_fields: sysevent volume by name and source
rules.detection_logic: Event sources whose volume exceeds threshold share of total
rules.evidence_to_show: Event volume by name and source, the flooding source, its trigger, and the queue depth during flood periods.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately high-volume events.

rules.rule: sys\_trigger backlog growing
rules.what_it_means: The sys_trigger backlog is growing.
rules.why_it_matters: Scheduled and async work is not being dispatched. Jobs run late or not at all, and the symptom appears as unrelated functional failures across the instance.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_trigger row counts, next action timestamps, backlog trend
rules.detection_logic: sys_trigger records with next action in the past, counted and trended
rules.evidence_to_show: Backlog count and trend, the oldest overdue trigger, the job types affected, and the worker capacity.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient backlog after a node restart.

rules.rule: Async job queue processing lag
rules.what_it_means: Async job queue processing lag exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Async work is queued rather than executed. Anything deferred to async — integrations, notifications, bulk updates — runs late, and the deferral was supposed to make things faster.
rules.source_tables_fields: Async queue depth and processing lag
rules.detection_logic: Async queue lag above threshold, trended
rules.evidence_to_show: Lag trend, queue depth, the job types queued, and the worker capacity and utilisation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient lag during a bulk operation.

rules.rule: Admin role count above threshold or trending up
rules.what_it_means: The admin role count exceeds threshold, or is trending upward.
rules.why_it_matters: Admin bypasses every ACL in the instance. The count is the single clearest measure of how much of the access control model is actually in force, and a rising trend means it is eroding.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_has_role for admin and equivalent roles, sys_user.active, trend across snapshots
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(active users holding admin, directly or through role nesting), with trend
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold relative to estate size; default 10 or 1% of fulfillers, whichever is lower
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the count after nesting resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Admin holder list with grant date, granting user, group path where nested, last login, and the trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Break-glass accounts that are documented and monitored.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — role removal is an access decision requiring approval
rules.cross_domain_link: The headline access finding; route to security and audit

rules.rule: ACLs with true as the condition or no condition at all
rules.what_it_means: ACLs exist with a condition of 'true' or no condition at all.
rules.why_it_matters: The ACL evaluates to permitted for everyone who reaches it. It appears in the ACL list as a control and grants unconditional access.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_security_acl condition and script fields
rules.detection_logic: Active ACLs with empty condition and empty script, or with a script returning true unconditionally
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; escalate on sensitive tables
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on empty conditions. 95% on unconditional script detection.
rules.evidence_to_show: ACL, table and field, operation, its condition and script, the roles required, and the record volume it governs.
rules.false_positive_guard: ACLs deliberately permissive where the role requirement is the control.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — condition addition as update set, tested carefully
rules.cross_domain_link: Ineffective access control presented as a control

rules.rule: Tables with no ACL coverage at all
rules.what_it_means: Tables exist with no ACL coverage at all.
rules.why_it_matters: Access falls back to a parent table ACL or to the default, neither of which was designed for this table. Custom tables holding sensitive data are the common case.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_db_object table list, sys_security_acl coverage with hierarchy resolution
rules.detection_logic: Tables with record volume and no ACL at table or field level, after parent inheritance resolution
rules.threshold_parameter: Inheritance resolution mandatory or this rule produces mass false positives
rules.confidence_basis: 100% after correct inheritance resolution. Resolution errors are the main failure mode — test it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, row count, ACL coverage state, the inherited ACLs applying, and the roles that can currently read and write.
rules.false_positive_guard: Coverage through parent inheritance that the resolution missed. Verify the resolution logic before raising at volume.
rules.cross_domain_link: Unintended access model on custom tables

rules.rule: Elevated privilege granted with no approval or change trail
rules.what_it_means: Elevated privilege has been granted with no approval or change trail.
rules.why_it_matters: Someone has admin or a high-privilege role and there is no record of who authorised it. In a regulated entity this is an audit exception independent of whether the grant was appropriate.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_has_role grant records and audit, change and approval record correlation
rules.detection_logic: Elevated role grants with no corresponding approval or change record in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Elevated role set configurable; correlation window configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on approval records being linkable to grants.
rules.evidence_to_show: The grant with date, granting user, recipient, the role, and the absence of approval or change lineage.
rules.false_positive_guard: Grants made through an approved bulk provisioning process.

rules.rule: Role nesting producing unintended effective permissions
rules.what_it_means: Role nesting produces effective permissions that were not intended.
rules.why_it_matters: A role three levels down contains admin. Nobody granting the outer role knew. Effective permissions diverge from stated permissions, and the divergence is invisible without traversing the graph.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_role_contains nesting graph, effective role resolution
rules.detection_logic: Roles whose transitive closure includes elevated roles not evident from the role name or description
rules.threshold_parameter: Elevated role set configurable; full transitive closure required
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the graph traversal. The judgement that it was unintended is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Role, its nesting path to the elevated role, the users holding it, and the effective permissions each gains.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate and documented nesting.
rules.cross_domain_link: Effective permissions diverge from stated permissions

rules.rule: ACL script returning true unconditionally
rules.what_it_means: An ACL script returns true unconditionally.
rules.why_it_matters: The narrower, harder-to-spot form of PLT-121. The ACL has a script, so it appears to implement logic, and the logic grants everything.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_security_acl script bodies, return path analysis
rules.detection_logic: ACL scripts whose every return path evaluates to true
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — return path analysis; complex scripts may be misjudged.
rules.evidence_to_show: ACL, the script, its return paths, the table and operation, and the record volume governed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scripts with conditional logic the analysis did not follow.

rules.rule: Write ACL absent where read ACL exists on sensitive tables
rules.what_it_means: A read ACL exists on a sensitive table with no corresponding write ACL.
rules.why_it_matters: Read is controlled and write is not. Anyone who reaches the table can modify it, which is the more damaging of the two operations.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_security_acl operation coverage by table, sensitive table classification
rules.detection_logic: Sensitive tables with read ACL coverage and no write, create or delete ACL
rules.threshold_parameter: Sensitive table set from classification or from DQ-139 detection
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on ACL coverage after inheritance resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, its sensitivity classification, the read ACLs present, the absent write ACLs, and the roles that can currently write.
rules.false_positive_guard: Write controlled through a data policy or business rule.

rules.rule: ACLs on sensitive fields (financial, personal, credential) missing
rules.what_it_means: Field-level ACLs are missing on sensitive fields — financial, personal or credential.
rules.why_it_matters: Table-level access grants the whole record including fields that should be restricted. Field-level protection is the mechanism for that and it is absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: Sensitive field classification, sys_security_acl field-level coverage
rules.detection_logic: Fields classified sensitive with no field-level ACL
rules.threshold_parameter: Sensitive field set from classification or content detection
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on ACL coverage. Field classification confidence depends on its source.
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, table, classification, absent field ACL, the table-level ACL in force, and the roles that can read it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Protection at table level genuinely adequate for that field.

rules.rule: snc\_internal or public-facing access on tables holding personal data
rules.what_it_means: Tables holding personal data are accessible via snc_internal or public-facing configuration.
rules.why_it_matters: Personal data reachable by the broadest access class on the instance, or by unauthenticated paths. The most serious access finding in the catalogue for a DPDP-regulated entity.
rules.source_tables_fields: Personal data table classification, ACL role requirements, public page and unauthenticated endpoint configuration
rules.detection_logic: Personal-data tables whose ACLs require only snc_internal, or which are reachable from public pages or unauthenticated endpoints
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on ACL role requirements. Public reachability at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, its personal data classification, record volume, the ACL role requirement, and the public or internal access path.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tables misclassified as holding personal data.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — escalate immediately, do not batch with routine findings
rules.cross_domain_link: Most serious DPDP access exposure; route to security immediately

rules.rule: Inactive users still holding roles
rules.what_it_means: Inactive users still hold roles.
rules.why_it_matters: Access persists after departure. The account cannot log in interactively but the role grant remains, which matters for API access, delegation, and if the account is ever reactivated.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user.active, sys_user_has_role
rules.detection_logic: Role grants held by users with active=false
rules.threshold_parameter: Report elevated roles separately from ordinary ones
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on user state and role grants.
rules.evidence_to_show: User list with deactivation date, the roles held, whether any are elevated, and any API or integration use of the account since.
rules.false_positive_guard: Accounts deactivated within a grace period pending formal offboarding.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — role removal is an access decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins DQ-117; access persistence after departure

rules.rule: Service accounts with interactive login enabled
rules.what_it_means: Service accounts have interactive login enabled.
rules.why_it_matters: A service account credential is typically long-lived, widely known within a team, and not subject to MFA. Interactive login on it removes the distinction between a service identity and a person.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user web_service_access_only flag, account type indicators, login history
rules.detection_logic: Accounts classified as service accounts with interactive login permitted
rules.threshold_parameter: Service account classification from naming, roles and usage pattern
rules.evidence_to_show: Account, its classification basis, interactive login configuration, login history, and the roles held.
rules.false_positive_guard: Accounts genuinely requiring interactive use.
rules.cross_domain_link: Identity model erosion; route to security

rules.rule: Roles granted directly to users rather than via groups
rules.what_it_means: Roles are granted directly to users rather than through groups.
rules.why_it_matters: Direct grants are invisible to group-based recertification and do not follow the person when they move. Access accumulates and is never reviewed.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_has_role grant source, group-derived versus direct
rules.detection_logic: Direct role grants as a share of total grants, by role and by user
rules.threshold_parameter: Report ratio and the elevated-role subset separately
rules.evidence_to_show: Direct grant ratio, the roles most commonly granted directly, the users holding them, and whether a group exists that would grant the same.
rules.false_positive_guard: Roles for which no appropriate group exists.

rules.rule: Roles with no users assigned
rules.what_it_means: Roles exist with no users assigned.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the role is obsolete, or it is a container in a nesting structure. Housekeeping, but a large population of empty roles makes access review harder.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_role records, sys_user_has_role counts, sys_user_role_contains
rules.detection_logic: Roles with zero direct and zero derived holders
rules.threshold_parameter: Exclude roles that are containers in an active nesting structure
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on holder counts after nesting resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Role list with creation date, nesting position, the ACLs referencing them, and holder count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Roles reserved for a future application.

rules.rule: Groups with no members holding elevated roles
rules.what_it_means: Groups holding elevated roles have no members.
rules.why_it_matters: The group is a live privilege container waiting for a member. Adding anyone to it grants elevated access without any role grant appearing in the audit trail.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_user_group records, group role grants, active membership
rules.detection_logic: Groups granting elevated roles with zero active members
rules.evidence_to_show: Group, the elevated roles it grants, membership history, last membership change, and who can add members.
rules.false_positive_guard: Break-glass groups documented and monitored.
rules.cross_domain_link: Latent privilege escalation path; route to security

rules.rule: No access recertification or review process evidenced
rules.what_it_means: No access recertification or review process is evidenced.
rules.why_it_matters: Access is granted and never reviewed. Every other access finding in this group accumulates because nothing removes it, which makes this the Systemic root of the access dimension.
rules.source_tables_fields: Recertification or attestation records for role and group membership, review task history
rules.detection_logic: Absence of recertification records covering role and group grants within a review period
rules.threshold_parameter: Review period from policy; default annual
rules.evidence_to_show: Recertification record state, the population that should be reviewed, grant ages, and the elevated role holders never reviewed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recertification conducted in an external IGA platform with evidence.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of access accumulation; regulatory evidence gap

rules.rule: ACL overriding an OOB ACL with weaker conditions
rules.what_it_means: A custom ACL overrides an out-of-box ACL with weaker conditions.
rules.why_it_matters: Platform protection replaced with something less restrictive. The OOB ACL was there for a reason and the reason is usually not documented in the replacement.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_security_acl records, OOB ACL inventory, condition comparison by table, field and operation
rules.detection_logic: Custom ACLs on the same table, field and operation as an OOB ACL, with weaker role or condition requirements
rules.threshold_parameter: Weakness comparison across role requirement and condition restrictiveness
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — relative restrictiveness comparison is partly a judgement.
rules.evidence_to_show: Custom ACL, the OOB ACL it shadows, both conditions and role requirements, and the access difference.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate and documented relaxation.

rules.rule: Impersonation used in production with no audit review
rules.what_it_means: Impersonation is used in production with no audit review.
rules.why_it_matters: One user acting as another. Legitimate for support, and it obscures attribution in the audit trail unless the impersonation records are themselves reviewed.
rules.source_tables_fields: Impersonation audit records, volume by impersonator and target, review evidence
rules.detection_logic: Impersonation events in production with no corresponding review record
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report volume by impersonator
rules.evidence_to_show: Impersonation volume by user, the targets, the actions taken while impersonating, and the absence of review.
rules.false_positive_guard: Impersonation reviewed through an external process.
rules.cross_domain_link: Attribution gap in the audit trail

rules.rule: Integration user holding admin role
rules.what_it_means: An integration user holds the admin role.
rules.why_it_matters: The credential is stored in an external system, often in configuration, and it grants unrestricted access. Compromise of any system holding it is compromise of the entire instance.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration user identification, sys_user_has_role, web service access configuration
rules.detection_logic: Users classified as integration accounts holding admin or equivalent
rules.threshold_parameter: Integration account classification from web_service_access_only, naming and usage
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — integration account classification is inferred but usually clear.
rules.evidence_to_show: Account, its classification basis, the admin grant with date and granting user, the systems using it, and the minimum role set its actual operations require.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely requires broad access. Recommend a scoped role set regardless.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — role reduction requires testing against the integration
rules.cross_domain_link: Highest-severity integration security finding; route to security

rules.rule: Basic authentication in use on any inbound or outbound integration
rules.what_it_means: Basic authentication is in use on inbound or outbound integrations.
rules.why_it_matters: Credentials transmitted on every call, typically long-lived and rarely rotated. For a regulated entity this is a control finding regardless of transport encryption.
rules.source_tables_fields: REST and SOAP message authentication configuration, inbound web service authentication
rules.detection_logic: Integrations configured with basic authentication
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report inbound and outbound separately
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, direction, endpoint, authentication type, call volume, and the OAuth capability available.
rules.false_positive_guard: Endpoints that support no other mechanism. Document and compensate.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security control finding; route to security

rules.rule: Credentials stored outside the credential vault
rules.what_it_means: Integration credentials are stored outside the credential vault.
rules.why_it_matters: Secrets in configuration tables rather than in a managed store. Captured in update sets, readable by anyone with the relevant table access, and not subject to rotation controls.
rules.source_tables_fields: Credential storage configuration, vault integration state, connection and credential alias usage
rules.detection_logic: Integrations with credentials stored inline rather than through a credential or connection alias
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires where vault or alias capability exists
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, credential storage mechanism, the vault capability available, and the roles that can read the stored value.
rules.false_positive_guard: No vault capability available. Report as a capability gap.

rules.rule: Inbound integration bypassing IRE or Data Policy
rules.what_it_means: Inbound integrations bypass the identification engine or data policies.
rules.why_it_matters: Data enters the platform without passing the controls designed to validate and reconcile it. The direct cause of a large share of CMDB duplicates and invalid values.
rules.source_tables_fields: Inbound integration write paths, IRE usage, data policy apply-to configuration
rules.detection_logic: Inbound integrations writing directly to tables without IRE processing or data policy application
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to tables where IRE or data policies exist
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, its write path, the tables, IRE and data policy bypass, the record volume created, and the duplicate and validity defects attributable.
rules.false_positive_guard: Bulk migration with deliberate bypass under a documented plan.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of CMDB-046 and CMDB-029

rules.rule: Integration with no error handling or retry
rules.what_it_means: An integration has no error handling or retry configuration.
rules.why_it_matters: A single transient failure produces a permanent data gap. With retry, the same failure self-heals and nobody needs to know.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration error handling and retry configuration
rules.detection_logic: Integrations with no retry or error handling configured
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, retry and error configuration, historical transient failure count, and the data gaps each produced.
rules.false_positive_guard: Semantics where retry is inappropriate, such as non-idempotent operations.

rules.rule: Integration failure rate above threshold
rules.what_it_means: Integration failure rate exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The integration is unreliable. Downstream data is incomplete in ways that are intermittent and therefore hard to characterise.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration execution outcomes, failure counts by integration
rules.detection_logic: Integrations with failure rate above threshold, ranked by failure volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, execution and failure counts, failure rate and trend, error classes, and the affected downstream data.
rules.false_positive_guard: Failures expected for some inputs.

rules.rule: Integration with no rate limiting configured
rules.what_it_means: An integration has no rate limiting configured.
rules.why_it_matters: An upstream system can flood the instance. A misbehaving integration partner becomes a platform availability event, and there is no mechanism to contain it.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_rate_limit_rule coverage, inbound integration volume
rules.detection_logic: Inbound integrations with no covering rate limit rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; escalate for high-volume or external-facing integrations
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, call volume and peak rate, absent rate limit coverage, and the transaction impact during peak periods.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rate limiting applied at an upstream gateway.

rules.rule: Endpoints using HTTP rather than HTTPS
rules.what_it_means: Integration endpoints use HTTP rather than HTTPS.
rules.why_it_matters: Data and credentials in plaintext across the network. Straightforward finding, and it still appears regularly on internal endpoints where people assume the network is trusted.
rules.source_tables_fields: REST and SOAP message endpoint URLs, protocol
rules.detection_logic: Integration endpoints with an http:// scheme
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, endpoint, direction, authentication type, call volume, and the data transmitted.
rules.false_positive_guard: Internal endpoints on a segmented network with documented acceptance.

rules.rule: OAuth tokens with no expiry or excessive lifetime
rules.what_it_means: OAuth tokens have no expiry, or an excessive lifetime.
rules.why_it_matters: A long-lived token is functionally a permanent credential with none of the controls a password carries. Revocation becomes the only mitigation and it is rarely exercised.
rules.source_tables_fields: oauth_entity and oauth_credential expiry configuration
rules.detection_logic: OAuth configurations with no token expiry or lifetime above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Lifetime threshold configurable; default 90 days for refresh tokens
rules.evidence_to_show: OAuth entity, token lifetime, the roles the token grants, the systems holding it, and the last rotation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Lifetime required by an external system's constraints.

rules.rule: Integration writing directly to tables, bypassing business logic
rules.what_it_means: An integration writes directly to tables, bypassing business logic.
rules.why_it_matters: Business rules, flows and data policies do not fire. Downstream effects that should follow the write do not happen, and the record is created in a state the process model does not expect.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration write paths, setWorkflow usage, direct table API usage
rules.detection_logic: Integrations writing with workflow suppressed or through paths that bypass business logic
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration, its write path, the suppressed logic, the tables, the record volume, and the downstream effects that do not occur.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate bypass for performance on a controlled bulk path.

rules.rule: Orphaned integrations with no execution in the window
rules.what_it_means: Orphaned integrations exist with no execution in the observation window.
rules.why_it_matters: Configured, credentialed and unused. Each one is an open door with no traffic, which is an access surface with no offsetting value.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration execution history, configuration records
rules.detection_logic: Integrations with no execution in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration list with last execution, credentials held, endpoint, and the roles the integration user holds.
rules.false_positive_guard: Seasonal or disaster-recovery integrations.

rules.rule: Duplicate integrations to the same endpoint
rules.what_it_means: Duplicate integrations point at the same endpoint.
rules.why_it_matters: Two configurations doing the same thing. Changes applied to one leave the other stale, and which one runs depends on what calls it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration endpoint URLs, method and payload comparison
rules.detection_logic: Integration pairs with matching endpoint and method
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — endpoint match is exact; the conclusion of unintended duplication is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both integrations, their endpoints, methods, callers, execution volumes, and configuration differences.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate separation by environment or purpose.

rules.rule: Import sets accumulating without cleanup
rules.what_it_means: Import set tables accumulate without cleanup.
rules.why_it_matters: Staging data retained indefinitely. Substantial table growth, and where the source data contains personal information it is a retention exposure as well.
rules.source_tables_fields: Import set table row counts and growth, cleanup job configuration
rules.detection_logic: Import set tables above size threshold with no cleanup job
rules.evidence_to_show: Import set tables with row counts, growth, oldest record, cleanup configuration, and whether the staged data includes personal identifiers.
rules.false_positive_guard: Retention required for reconciliation evidence.

rules.rule: Transform maps with no coalesce, generating duplicates
rules.what_it_means: Transform maps have no coalesce field configured, generating duplicate records on every run.
rules.why_it_matters: Every import creates new records instead of updating existing ones. On a recurring import this produces duplicates at a predictable rate, and it is one of the most mechanical causes of CMDB duplication.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_transform_map and sys_transform_entry coalesce configuration, target table duplicate counts
rules.detection_logic: Transform maps with no coalesce entry, joined to duplicate counts on their target tables
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence on a recurring import
rules.evidence_to_show: Transform map, its entries, absent coalesce, import frequency, and the duplicate record count on the target table.
rules.false_positive_guard: Insert-only maps where duplication is intended.

rules.rule: Transform scripts with unhandled errors
rules.what_it_means: Transform scripts throw unhandled errors.
rules.why_it_matters: Rows fail to transform and are silently skipped. The import reports completion with a lower row count than the source, and nobody reconciles the two.
rules.source_tables_fields: Transform script errors in the import log, error counts by map
rules.detection_logic: Transform maps with script error counts above threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Transform map, error count and class, sample errors, rows skipped, and the source-to-target row count reconciliation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Errors from genuinely malformed source rows.

rules.rule: Data source credentials expired
rules.what_it_means: Data source credentials have expired.
rules.why_it_matters: The import stops. Data ages from that date, and because the import job still runs and reports completion, nothing signals the failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_data_source credential references, credential expiry, import execution outcomes
rules.detection_logic: Data sources whose credentials are expired or failing authentication
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on credential state and import outcomes.
rules.evidence_to_show: Data source, credential state and expiry, last successful import, and the data now ageing as a result.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential rotation in progress.
rules.cross_domain_link: Silent import cessation; same pattern as ITOM-017

rules.rule: Integration with no documented owner
rules.what_it_means: An integration has no documented owner.
rules.why_it_matters: When it breaks, or when its access needs reviewing, nobody knows whose it is. Integrations outlive the people who build them more reliably than any other object type.
rules.source_tables_fields: Integration owner fields, created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Integrations with no owner, or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.evidence_to_show: Integration list with owner state, endpoint, execution volume, the roles its user holds, and creation date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership at application level.

rules.rule: Skipped updates from the last upgrade never reviewed
rules.what_it_means: Skipped updates from the last upgrade have never been reviewed.
rules.why_it_matters: At every upgrade, ServiceNow skips updates to records the customer modified. Each skipped update is a platform improvement or fix the instance did not receive, and the list is usually never opened.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_upgrade_history and sys_upgrade_history_log, skipped update records and review state
rules.detection_logic: Skipped updates from the most recent upgrade with no review disposition recorded
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unreviewed skipped update; rank by the object's execution volume and criticality
rules.evidence_to_show: Skipped update list ranked by object criticality, the customisation causing each skip, the platform change that was skipped, and the review state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Reviews conducted outside ServiceNow with evidence.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — each disposition is a judgement
rules.cross_domain_link: The single richest source of upgrade debt evidence

rules.rule: Modified OOB records count and trend
rules.what_it_means: The count of modified out-of-box records, and its trend.
rules.why_it_matters: The headline customisation measure. The trend matters more than the count: an estate adding modifications faster than it retires them is accumulating upgrade cost that compounds at every release.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_update_version and sys_metadata OOB modification indicators, trend across snapshots
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(OOB records with customer modifications), by object type, with trend
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by object type; no single threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Modified OOB count by object type, trend, the objects most modified, and the skipped update count each has generated.
rules.false_positive_guard: Modifications required by a genuine functional gap.

rules.rule: Customization concentrated in objects ServiceNow actively develops
rules.what_it_means: Customisation is concentrated in objects that ServiceNow actively develops.
rules.why_it_matters: Modifying a stable object is low risk. Modifying one ServiceNow changes every release guarantees a collision at every upgrade, forever. Concentration here is what makes upgrades expensive.
rules.source_tables_fields: Modified OOB records, ServiceNow change frequency per object across releases
rules.detection_logic: Modified OOB objects ranked by the platform's own change frequency for that object
rules.threshold_parameter: Change frequency derived from upgrade history across releases
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — change frequency derivation depends on upgrade history depth available.
rules.evidence_to_show: Modified objects ranked by platform change frequency, the skipped updates each has produced, and the projected collisions at the next upgrade.
rules.false_positive_guard: Modifications to objects the platform rarely changes.

rules.rule: Instance more than two families behind current
rules.what_it_means: The instance is more than two families behind the current release.
rules.why_it_matters: Support, security patches and feature availability all degrade. Each additional family behind makes the eventual upgrade larger and the collision count higher.
rules.source_tables_fields: Instance version and family, current ServiceNow release
rules.detection_logic: Instance family compared against current, in family count
rules.evidence_to_show: Instance family, current family, families behind, last upgrade date, and the skipped update backlog.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate deferral with documented support arrangements.
rules.cross_domain_link: Compounding upgrade cost and support exposure

rules.rule: Global scope customization where scoped apps should be used
rules.what_it_means: Global scope customisation exists where scoped applications should have been used.
rules.why_it_matters: Global has no boundary, no dependency declaration and no containment. Customisation there is invisible to application-level governance and collides more readily at upgrade.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom object scope distribution, scoped application inventory
rules.detection_logic: Custom objects in global scope that form a coherent functional group suitable for a scoped application
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — the judgement that they belong in a scope is inferential.
rules.evidence_to_show: Global custom object inventory grouped by function, their tables, and the scoped applications that exist.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely cross-cutting platform extensions.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — scope migration is a programme

rules.rule: Custom tables extending task or cmdb\_ci without justification
rules.what_it_means: Custom tables extend task or cmdb_ci without justification.
rules.why_it_matters: Extending task inherits the entire task lifecycle, SLA engine and business rule cascade. Extending cmdb_ci inherits identification, reconciliation and health. Both are appropriate sometimes and expensive when they are not.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_db_object super_class, custom table identification, usage analysis
rules.detection_logic: Custom tables extending task or cmdb_ci whose usage does not exercise the inherited capabilities
rules.threshold_parameter: Usage assessment from field population and process linkage
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — whether the extension is justified is a design judgement.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, its parent, row count, the inherited capabilities, which are actually used, and the rules and SLAs cascading to it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Extensions that genuinely use the inherited model.

rules.rule: Custom fields on OOB tables, unpopulated
rules.what_it_means: Custom fields on out-of-box tables are unpopulated.
rules.why_it_matters: Schema weight, form clutter and upgrade review surface for data nobody captures. Each one must be assessed at every upgrade.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom fields on OOB tables, population rates
rules.detection_logic: Custom fields on OOB tables with population rate below threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Field list with table, population rate, creation date, creating update set, and the forms carrying it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Fields for a programme not yet live.

rules.rule: Custom fields duplicating OOB field function
rules.what_it_means: Custom fields duplicate the function of an existing out-of-box field.
rules.why_it_matters: Two fields hold the same thing. Reporting splits, integrations pick one, and the platform features that read the OOB field see nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom field definitions, OOB field semantics on the same table, population correlation
rules.detection_logic: Custom fields whose semantics and population correlate with an existing OOB field on the same table
rules.threshold_parameter: Semantic matching from name, type and population correlation
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — semantic equivalence is inferential. Report both fields for human comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both fields, their types, population rates and correlation, and the platform features reading the OOB field.
rules.false_positive_guard: Custom field capturing a genuinely distinct attribute.
rules.cross_domain_link: Split data; platform features read the wrong field

rules.rule: Deprecated API usage in scripts
rules.what_it_means: Scripts use deprecated APIs.
rules.why_it_matters: Deprecated APIs are removed eventually. The script works until the release that removes them, and the failure arrives as part of an upgrade with many other changes.
rules.source_tables_fields: Script bodies across all script object types, deprecated API inventory for the instance version
rules.detection_logic: Scripts containing calls to APIs marked deprecated in the current or announced releases
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on the deprecation list being current.
rules.evidence_to_show: Script, the deprecated API, the release in which it was deprecated, the removal release where announced, and the script's execution volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: APIs deprecated with no announced removal.

rules.rule: Deprecated plugin still active
rules.what_it_means: Deprecated plugins remain active.
rules.why_it_matters: The plugin is no longer developed and may be removed. Functionality built on it is on borrowed time, and the migration path narrows each release.
rules.source_tables_fields: v_plugin active list, deprecation status per instance version
rules.detection_logic: Active plugins marked deprecated
rules.threshold_parameter: Deprecation status from the instance's own plugin metadata
rules.evidence_to_show: Plugin, deprecation status, the functionality depending on it, usage volume, and the replacement path.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deprecated plugin with no replacement available.

rules.rule: Customization hotspots — objects modified repeatedly
rules.what_it_means: Customisation hotspots — objects modified repeatedly over time.
rules.why_it_matters: Repeated modification indicates either an unstable requirement or a design that does not fit. Hotspots are where upgrade collisions concentrate and where defects are most likely.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_update_version modification counts per object, trend
rules.detection_logic: Objects with modification counts above threshold across the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Object ranked by modification count, the modifying users and update sets, the skipped updates produced, and the incident correlation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Objects under active development in a live project.
rules.cross_domain_link: Where upgrade collisions and defects concentrate

rules.rule: Update sets unclosed, stuck in preview, or with collisions
rules.what_it_means: Update sets are unclosed, stuck in preview, or carrying unresolved collisions.
rules.why_it_matters: Changes are held in limbo. Unclosed sets can lose changes on capture, preview-stuck sets block promotion, and unresolved collisions mean somebody will eventually force a promotion and overwrite something.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_update_set state, sys_remote_update_set preview state, collision records
rules.detection_logic: Update sets in open state beyond age threshold, in preview beyond threshold, or with unresolved collisions
rules.threshold_parameter: Age thresholds configurable; report the three cases separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on set state and collision records.
rules.evidence_to_show: Update set list by state with age, owner, record count, and the collision details for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Sets deliberately held open for an active project.
rules.cross_domain_link: Release process blockage and overwrite risk

rules.rule: Changes made directly in production with no update set lineage
rules.what_it_means: Changes have been made directly in production with no update set lineage.
rules.why_it_matters: The release process was bypassed entirely. No test evidence, no approval, no rollback, and no record of the prior state. The platform-layer equivalent of ITSM-106.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_metadata records, sys_update_xml lineage, creation timestamps and instance indicators
rules.detection_logic: Customisation records with no update set lineage, by object type and creation window
rules.threshold_parameter: Report count, trend and distribution by creating user
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — lineage absence is strong evidence; update set records can be purged.
rules.evidence_to_show: Object list with creation date and user, absent lineage, the change records in those windows, and the distribution by user.
rules.false_positive_guard: Lineage purged by retention. Check the retention window before asserting.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITSM-106 and PLT-060; direct change control bypass

rules.rule: Cross-scope access requests granted broadly
rules.what_it_means: Cross-scope access requests have been granted broadly.
rules.why_it_matters: Scoped applications exist to contain. Broad cross-scope grants dissolve the containment while leaving the appearance of a scoped architecture intact.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_scope_privilege records, grant scope and target breadth
rules.detection_logic: Cross-scope privileges granted at table or application level where a narrower grant would suffice
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — the judgement that a narrower grant would suffice is inferred from usage.
rules.evidence_to_show: The privilege, granting and target scope, the breadth granted, the actual usage, and the narrower grant that would cover it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Broad access genuinely required.

rules.rule: Custom application with no owner or no source control
rules.what_it_means: A custom application has no owner, or no source control linkage.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody owns it and there is no version history outside the instance. Recovery from a bad change depends entirely on update set history.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_app records, owner fields, source control configuration
rules.detection_logic: Custom applications with no owner or no source control repository linked
rules.evidence_to_show: Application list with owner state, source control linkage, object count, and last modification date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source control maintained externally without linkage.

rules.rule: Table sprawl — custom tables with zero or near-zero records
rules.what_it_means: Custom tables exist with zero or near-zero records.
rules.why_it_matters: Built for a purpose that never materialised. Each adds schema weight, ACL surface and upgrade review cost for no return.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom table row counts, creation dates
rules.detection_logic: Custom tables with row count below threshold and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Row threshold default 5; age threshold default 180 days
rules.evidence_to_show: Table list with row count, creation date, creating application, the ACLs and rules attached, and the forms built on it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tables for a programme not yet live.

rules.rule: Extension depth beyond recommended
rules.what_it_means: Table extension depth exceeds the recommended maximum.
rules.why_it_matters: Deep hierarchies make attribute inheritance hard to reason about and slow class-based queries. Each level adds join cost to every query against the child.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_db_object super_class chains, depth measurement
rules.detection_logic: Tables whose extension depth exceeds threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Table hierarchy with depth, row counts at each level, the custom levels, and the query performance on the deepest children.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deep OOB hierarchies shipped by the platform.

rules.rule: Transaction response time 95th percentile beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: Transaction response time at the 95th percentile exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The measure users actually experience. The mean hides the tail, and the tail is what generates complaints and support tickets.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog_transaction response times, percentile calculation by transaction type
rules.detection_logic: 95th percentile response time by transaction type and overall, against threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold configurable; default 3 seconds for interactive transactions
rules.evidence_to_show: 95th percentile by transaction type, trend, the slowest transaction types, and the scripts attributed to each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Batch and administrative transactions in the same population. Segment interactive from non-interactive.

rules.rule: Slow transaction count trending up
rules.what_it_means: Slow transaction count is trending upward.
rules.why_it_matters: Direction matters more than the absolute number. A rising trend means something is degrading, and the trend usually predates the complaints by weeks.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog_transaction slow transaction counts across windows
rules.detection_logic: Slow transaction count per period, trended, normalised by total transaction volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires at least 3 windows; normalisation is mandatory or growth in usage reads as degradation
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from window count. State the normalisation applied.
rules.evidence_to_show: Slow transaction count trend normalised by volume, the transaction types contributing most to the growth, and the changes in those windows.
rules.false_positive_guard: Usage growth without normalisation. Always normalise.
rules.cross_domain_link: Leading indicator, typically weeks ahead of complaints

rules.rule: Specific scripts appearing repeatedly in slow transaction traces
rules.what_it_means: Specific scripts appear repeatedly in slow transaction traces.
rules.why_it_matters: The ranked attribution that turns performance work from guesswork into a queue. A handful of scripts usually account for the majority of measured slow time.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog_transaction script attribution, aggregation by script
rules.detection_logic: Scripts appearing in slow traces, ranked by total attributed time
rules.threshold_parameter: Report both frequency and total time; total time is the better ranking
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where transaction data attributes scripts. Attribution completeness varies by instance — state it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ranked script list with occurrence count, average and total attributed time, the transaction types, and the anti-patterns each contains.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attribution unavailable on some configurations. Report the limitation rather than inferring.
rules.cross_domain_link: The performance remediation queue; joins PLT-052

rules.rule: Tables above size threshold with no rotation or archival
rules.what_it_means: Tables above a size threshold have no rotation or archival configured.
rules.why_it_matters: Unbounded growth with no exit. Query cost rises continuously, and for tables holding personal data there is a retention obligation with no mechanism behind it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Table row counts and growth, rotation and archival configuration
rules.detection_logic: Tables above size threshold with no rotation or archival rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Size threshold configurable; default 10 million rows or the top decile
rules.evidence_to_show: Table list with row count, growth rate, projected size, rotation configuration state, and whether the table holds personal data.
rules.false_positive_guard: Archival handled by an external process.
rules.cross_domain_link: Query cost and DPDP retention; joins DQ-136

rules.rule: Queries on large tables without supporting indexes
rules.what_it_means: Queries run against large tables without supporting indexes.
rules.why_it_matters: The specific, fixable cause behind most slow transactions. An index on the right column is a contained update set and often a dramatic improvement.
rules.source_tables_fields: Table row counts, index definitions, query predicates from transaction and slow query data
rules.detection_logic: High-frequency query predicates on large tables with no supporting index
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — index recommendations depend on query pattern sampling being representative.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table, row count, the frequent predicates, existing indexes, the proposed index, and the transactions that would benefit.
rules.false_positive_guard: Index deliberately omitted for write-cost reasons.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — index creation via update set, tested first
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct remediation for PLT-171 and PLT-173

rules.rule: sys\_audit and history tables growing without rotation
rules.what_it_means: sys_audit and history tables are growing without rotation.
rules.why_it_matters: These grow faster than the data they describe and are queried rarely. Unbounded growth here is both a performance cost and, where the audited records contain personal data, a retention exposure.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_audit, sys_history_line and sys_history_set row counts and growth, rotation configuration
rules.detection_logic: Audit and history tables above size threshold with no rotation configured
rules.evidence_to_show: Table sizes, growth rates, oldest record, rotation configuration, and the audit retention requirement.
rules.false_positive_guard: Retention required for a longer period than default by regulation.

rules.rule: Attachment storage growth beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: Attachment storage growth exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Storage cost and instance size. Attachments also carry the content that DQ-135 flags, so growth here is an exposure trend as well as a cost one.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_attachment and sys_attachment_doc sizes and growth
rules.detection_logic: Attachment storage volume and growth rate against threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Storage volume and growth, distribution by table and file type, the largest attachments, and the oldest.
rules.false_positive_guard: Growth from a documented content migration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Storage cost; joins DQ-135 exposure trend

rules.rule: Email queue backlog
rules.what_it_means: The email queue has a backlog.
rules.why_it_matters: Notifications are delayed. During an incident the notification that matters arrives after the event it was meant to warn about.
rules.source_tables_fields: sys_email queue state, age distribution
rules.detection_logic: Email queue depth and oldest-message age against thresholds
rules.evidence_to_show: Queue depth and age trend, message type distribution, send rate versus generation rate, and the notification types delayed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient backlog during a bulk send.

rules.rule: Semaphore exhaustion indicators
rules.what_it_means: Semaphore exhaustion indicators are present.
rules.why_it_matters: Semaphores are the instance's concurrency limit. Exhaustion means transactions queue or are rejected, and the effect is instance-wide rather than confined to the cause.
rules.source_tables_fields: Semaphore metrics where available, transaction cancellation and queuing indicators
rules.detection_logic: Semaphore exhaustion events or sustained high utilisation
rules.threshold_parameter: Thresholds from the instance's semaphore configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — semaphore-level detail is not fully exposed through customer-accessible APIs. State the inference basis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Exhaustion events with timing, the transactions holding semaphores longest, and the scripts attributed to them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Detail unavailable on this instance. Report the limitation rather than inferring from indirect signals alone.

rules.rule: Long-running transactions cancelled by the platform
rules.what_it_means: Long-running transactions are being cancelled by the platform.
rules.why_it_matters: The transaction hit the platform limit and was killed. The user sees a failure and the work is partially complete, which is worse than a clean rejection.
rules.source_tables_fields: syslog_transaction cancellation records, duration at cancellation
rules.detection_logic: Transactions cancelled by the platform, grouped by type and attributed script
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report frequency and trend
rules.evidence_to_show: Cancellation count by transaction type, the attributed scripts, the tables involved, and the affected users.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cancellations from deliberate administrative termination.

rules.rule: List and report queries returning excessive row counts
rules.what_it_means: List and report queries return excessive row counts.
rules.why_it_matters: Large result sets consume memory and transaction time for data nobody reads past the first page. Common in saved filters and scheduled reports nobody reviewed.
rules.source_tables_fields: Transaction data for list and report queries, returned row counts
rules.detection_logic: List and report queries returning row counts above threshold
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where row counts are recorded in transaction data.
rules.evidence_to_show: Query, the list or report, row count, execution frequency, the user or schedule triggering it, and the transaction time.
rules.false_positive_guard: Exports genuinely requiring the full set.

rules.rule: Homepages and dashboards with expensive widgets
rules.what_it_means: Homepages and dashboards contain expensive widgets.
rules.why_it_matters: Every load runs every widget. A dashboard opened by two hundred people each morning multiplies its cost by two hundred, and the cost is invisible because it is distributed.
rules.source_tables_fields: Homepage and dashboard widget definitions, widget query cost from transaction data, view volume
rules.detection_logic: Widgets whose query cost exceeds threshold, ranked by cost multiplied by view volume
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — widget-level attribution depends on transaction data granularity.
rules.evidence_to_show: Dashboard, the expensive widgets, their queries and cost, view volume, and the total attributed time.
rules.false_positive_guard: Dashboards with low view volume.
rules.cross_domain_link: Distributed cost multiplied by view volume

rules.rule: Scheduled reports running during peak hours
rules.what_it_means: Scheduled reports run during peak hours.
rules.why_it_matters: Reporting competes with interactive users for the same capacity. The report does not need to run then and the users cannot choose to wait.
rules.source_tables_fields: Scheduled report execution times, transaction volume distribution by hour
rules.detection_logic: Scheduled reports executing during peak transaction windows
rules.threshold_parameter: Peak window derived from the instance's own transaction volume distribution
rules.evidence_to_show: Report, schedule time, the peak window, its query cost, and the transaction performance during those windows.
rules.false_positive_guard: Reports that genuinely require peak-time data.
